items.title: Budget européen et financement de Kiev : les divisions entre États membres écourtent le sommet de Bruxelles
items.description: La deuxieme journee du sommet de l'Union europeenne a Bruxelles, prevue ce 27 novembre, a ete annulee apres l'echec des negociations sur le budget pour 2028-2034 et le financement de Kiev pour 2027. La rencontre, organisee a l'initiative du president du Conseil europeen, Antonio Costa, devait permettre de rapprocher les positions des etats membres sur un projet de budget initialement estime a pres de 2 000 milliards d'euros. Elle a finalement ete marquee par des tensions, des reproches mutuels et des boycotts. Alors que 17 etats, dont l'Italie et l'Espagne, defendent le maintien des aides agricoles et des fonds destines aux regions les moins favorisees, sept pays, parmi lesquels l'Allemagne et la Suede, reclament une reduction du budget global et une reorientation des depenses vers les secteurs militaire et securitaire. La reduction de 204 milliards d'euros proposee par Antonio Costa n'a satisfait aucun des deux camps. Selon Politico, les sept pays favorables a une baisse du budget ont boycotte les consultations en groupes restreints, denoncant une tentative de les diviser. Macron accuse de chantage sur fond d'echeances electorales Alors que l'UE dispose encore de temps pour adopter son budget, Emmanuel Macron exige un accord d'ici au 31 decembre, invoquant la proximite de la presidentielle francaise de 2027. Marine Le Pen, en tete des sondages, s'est engagee a mettre fin au financement de l'Ukraine et a reduire considerablement la contribution francaise au budget communautaire. Les pressions exercees par Macron ont suscite de vives critiques. Un responsable europeen l'a surnomme « Monsieur Chantage », rapporte Politico , tandis qu'un diplomate lui a reproche de prendre les negociations en otage pour des considerations electorales nationales. La Premiere ministre italienne Giorgia Meloni a, pour sa part, ecarte toute echeance imposee, affirmant qu'elle ne signerait qu'un accord qu'elle jugerait equitable pour son pays. Berlin accentue la pression sur les etats opposes au financement de Kiev Le projet de nouveau credit de 45 milliards d'euros destine a Kiev pour 2027 se heurte toujours a l'opposition de la Hongrie, de la Slovaquie et de la Republique tcheque. Le chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz avait menace de bloquer le prochain budget europeen si certains etats refusaient de participer a ce financement. Cette menace lui a valu des accusations de chantage de la part du Premier ministre slovaque Robert Fico. Berlin cherche egalement a faire adopter les futures decisions relatives au financement de Kiev a la majorite plutot qu'a l'unanimite, privant ainsi chaque etat membre de la possibilite d'exercer seul son droit de veto. Alors que les Europeens se disputent sur le maintien des subventions agricoles et regionales, le projet de budget pour 2028-2034 prevoit toujours d'allouer jusqu'a 100 milliards d'euros a l'Ukraine. Les negociations reprendront le 17 decembre, sans garantie d'un accord avant la fin de l'annee.

items.title: 11 years on, Abetifi District Hospital lies abandoned as Kwahu residents appeal to Mahama
items.description: What was envisioned as a major boost to healthcare delivery in the Kwahu enclave 11 years ago now lies abandoned, with weeds taking over the site and once-promising structures deteriorating. The 120-bed Abetifi District Hospital, which has the capacity to be expanded to 200 beds, remains incomplete despite being one of six turnkey hospital projects awarded in 2015. While the other five projects have been completed and operationalised, the Abetifi project has remained stalled, leaving residents of Abetifi and surrounding communities in the Kwahu East District frustrated and disappointed. The other projects included the Dodowa District Hospital, Adansi North District Hospital at Fomena, Sekyere Kumawu District Hospital at Kumawu, and Garu Timpane Hospital in the Upper East Region. For residents, the uncompleted hospital has become a painful reminder of a promise yet to be fulfilled. Former District Chief Executive (DCE) for Kwahu East, Samuel Asamoah, who is now back in office, said the project was conceived during his previous tenure around 2014 and 2015. Flashback: The Abetifi District Hospital then He said the Kwahu District Assembly secured the land for the project through the generosity of traditional authorities, who donated it without charge. “First of all, let me say that this Abetifi Referral Hospital started during my time as DCE, around 2014 and 2015. The whole idea, you know, started around that time. And I led the Kwahu District Assembly to secure land from Nananom. To be honest with you, Nananom gave the land to the assembly free of charge. We didn’t even pay a pesewa,” he said. Contractors, NMS Infrastructure, moved to the site in 2015 amid fanfare after the government, through the Ministry of Health, compensated farmers for crops on the land to make way for construction. However, work stalled following the change of government in 2016, when the project was estimated to be between 35 and 40 per cent complete. The transition from the John Mahama-led National Democratic Congress (NDC) administration to the New Patriotic Party (NPP) government brought construction to a halt, leaving the partially completed structures exposed to the elements for years. Although the contractor has maintained a presence at the site, there is no active construction. Abandoned staff bungalow Farmers regret losing their land The prolonged abandonment has also left farmers who surrendered their farmlands for the project regretting their decision. Nana Addo Opambuor is one of them. He said he was disappointed that fertile farmland had been taken over by a project that had remained incomplete for more than a decade. “I am disappointed to lose my fertile land to an abandoned hospital project. I feel sad anytime I see the state of the project. If we were allowed to cultivate cassava during these lost years, it would have benefited us greatly. Now, see how I have grown lean because we are unable to farm on our land,” he lamented. Another resident, Kaakyire Badu, who witnessed the sod-cutting ceremony, expressed similar disappointment. “I am not happy at the sorry state of the hospital project. The new government that took over abandoned it. It is in ruins now,” he said. Assemblyman for Dome-Kubease-Christian Quarters-Odwenase, Agyapong Boahene, also shared the concerns of residents and appealed to President Mahama to intervene. “If you go there, nobody is working there. I can say that it is now in a deplorable state because nothing is happening over there. And it’s unfortunate. We are pleading on behalf of the people to President Mahama. We are all Ghanaians. Yes, we too deserve better. So, we are appealing,” he said. Change of government brought construction to a halt Mr Asamoah, who played a key role in securing the land and initiating the project during his previous tenure as DCE, said construction had reached between 35 and 40 per cent before the change of government. He expressed disappointment that the succeeding administration failed to continue the project during its eight years in office. “The project started. We cleared the land, and the project started. If my memory serves me right, we covered up to about, I mean, between 35 to 40%. It was between 35 and 40% complete until, in 2016, latter part of 2016, the NDC government lost power, and the NPP came. “The expectation was that the government then would continue with the project. But unfortunately, for eight years, nothing was done over there,” he said. Local authorities say the prolonged inactivity has heightened concerns among residents in Abetifi, other parts of Kwahu and neighbouring communities. Samuel Asamoah is DCE, Kwahu East Although structural integrity assessments have been conducted on the abandoned facility, uncertainty remains over how much of the existing infrastructure can be salvaged. Mr Asamoah said the African Engineering and Structural Services Limited (AESSL) team conducted an assessment, while another structural integrity test was undertaken in 2023. He said a report he obtained after assuming office indicated that some portions of the structures were weak, while others could still be continued. Abetifi High Street “An AESSL team came around to make the necessary assessment. And then I think around 2023, NPP also conducted structural integrity tests on the structures over there. I fortunately got a copy of the report when I came in as DCE. “And if you look at it, the indication is that some of the structures are weak; others can be continued. So whatever it is, if proper structural assessment is done on it, and there’s a need for the government to continue, this government will continue. If there’s a need for the government to start everything afresh,” he said. Residents want a government-owned referral hospital Although the Kwahu enclave has healthcare facilities such as the Holy Family Hospital at Nkawkaw, Atibie Hospital and Donkorkrom Presbyterian Hospital, residents say the completion of the Abetifi facility would provide an important addition to healthcare delivery in the area. The existing facilities are mission-run or privately managed, making the proposed government-owned hospital particularly significant to the people. The Abetifi District Hospital was envisioned as a major referral centre that would serve the wider Kwahu area and neighbouring communities, including those in the Afram Plains, while helping to ease pressure on major facilities such as Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, Korle Bu Teaching Hospital and the Eastern Regional Hospital in Koforidua. Mr Asamoah said the project was particularly significant because it would have marked the first district hospital built by a government specifically for the people of Kwahu. “If you trace the history of this project, when it started, it was like—once the government completes this referral hospital project—it would have been the first district hospital any government of Ghana is building for the people of Kwahu,” he said. DCE appeals to Mahama to resume work With the NDC back in government, Mr Asamoah is hopeful that the project will finally be completed. He disclosed that he had already engaged the Chief of Staff, Julius Debrah, and the Minister of Health in separate meetings to discuss the hospital’s future. He is now appealing directly to President Mahama, whose administration initiated the project, to prioritise its completion. “I want to use your media to appeal to the President, to the government, to, as a matter of urgency, try to come back quickly to help us complete the project. I trust my President, I trust the government, I trust my Chief of Staff. And I know that for sure this project will be done. This project will be done,” he said. For the DCE, completing the hospital would bring considerable relief and renewed hope to residents who have waited more than a decade for the facility. “I want to use this media to appeal to the President that this referral hospital is something the entire Kwahu is looking forward to having completed. And it is something which will bring happiness to the people of Kwahu,” he added. Eleven years after construction began, the Abetifi District Hospital remains unfinished, its deteriorating structures standing as a reminder of a project that has outlived two administrations. For the people of Kwahu, the hope is that the latest appeal will finally translate into a return of construction workers to the site and the completion of a hospital they have waited so long to see.

items.title: Man buried under rubble rescued alive 2 days after building collapse in Karachi’s Baloch Colony
items.description: KARACHI: A man buried under the rubble from the collapse of an under-construction six-storey building near Karachi’s Baloch Colony was rescued alive on Friday, two days after the incident occurred. On Wednesday, three people were killed and 14 others injured when the under-construction building — reportedly being constructed illegally on a residential plot — collapsed . Another body was recovered on Thursday, taking the death toll to four. On Friday, four more bodies were recovered, taking the toll to eight. Rescue 1122 said on Friday that 28-year-old Muhammad Adil was rescued alive from the rubble. It said that the search operation for any other individuals feared trapped was underway. Its spokesperson, Hassaanul Haseeb Khan, termed the rescue a “breakthrough”. He added that rescue operations were ongoing to search for other survivors from the debris. He said the rescued man told them that two other persons who might be alive were in touch with him. However, Khan said the rescuers conducted a search in the identified area but could not locate them. Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah expressed gratitude that the man trapped under the rubble survived for 54 hours, describing it as a “miracle”, according to a statement issued from his office. According to the statement, the chief minister directed rescue agencies and the Karachi commissioner to accelerate the ongoing rescue operation and deploy all available resources. Murad also praised rescue workers for their tireless efforts and directed officials to ensure the survivor receives the best possible medical treatment. The statement added that CM Murad had ordered a comprehensive investigation into the building collapse, warning that action would be taken against those found responsible for negligence. Death toll rises to 8 In a separate statement, Rescue 1122 said the total number of bodies recovered from the rubble had reached eight. The service’s spokesperson told Dawn that 11 people were still missing according to reports submitted by their relatives at the information desk set up at the site of the collapsed building. He said it may not be advisable for the workers to provide a timeline for finishing the rescue and debris removal operation at this stage. Khan said that heavy machinery was also being used to remove debris, but that whenever a human body was spotted in the debris, the team stopped the machine operations and initiated manual work with extra care to recover the body. He admitted that this pace of the rescue operation may be causing concern for the relatives of the missing persons, who were protesting the slowness of the operation. Newly-appointed East Deputy Commissioner Kashif Nabi Khuhro, speaking to the media, denied that the pace of the rescue operation was slow. However, he pointed out that the collapsed building was situated in congested and narrow streets, where it was relatively difficult to move heavy machinery. Sindh Local Government Secretary Waseem Shamshad, who also served as director general of the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA), was removed from both posts on Thursday on the directives of CM Murad following the incident. The CM ordered sweeping action over the incident while chairing a high-level meeting, further issuing directives for the removal of East Deputy Commissioner Nasrullah Abbasi, as well as Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) East Zubair Sheikh over “negligence”, a statement issued by the CM Office said. In addition to the removal of the three officials, CM Murad further issued directives for the suspension of 16 SBCA officials and the initiation of an inquiry against them. He directed the police to “immediately” arrest the building’s owner, Salman Tahir, and the builder, Zeeshan. Moreover, he instructed that the building’s architect and structural engineer be included in the incident’s investigation to determine whether the construction complied with approved plans, building regulations and safety standards. 14 ‘illegal’ buildings in KAEHS to be demolished The KDA’s Additional Deputy DG Farhan Kaiser visited the site on Thursday and told the media that their first priority was to remove the debris. He said that under the directions of the Sindh CM and LG minister, “illegal buildings” were being sealed across the metropolis. He said that so far, 14 buildings had been sealed in the KAEHS after the building collapse and would be demolished in a second phase of the operation. Kaiser added that it was the responsibility of the residents to report illegal buildings in their respective areas, and vowed to take action against the builders and owners of these buildings. Members of the Chief Minister Inspection Team (CMIT), Bilal Memon and Anwar Shar, visited the scene and collected samples of the material used in the construction of the building for investigation purposes. Rehabilitation secretary Rafiq Mustafa Shaikh, SBCA DG Abid Saleem, Rescue 1122 DG Brig. (retd) Wajid Sibghatullah Mahar and Rescue 1122 COO Dr Abid Jalaluddin Shaikh also visited the site and supervised the rescue operation. FIR registered A first information report (FIR) of the incident was registered at the Tipu Sultan police station on Wednesday, on the complaint of an official of the Sindh Local Government Department. The FIR, seen by Dawn , invoked Sections 302 (intentional murder), 119 (public servant concealing design to commit offence), 427 (mischief causing damage), 337-H(1) (hurt caused by rash or negligent act), 109 (abetment) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code. The building’s four owners — including Salman Tahir whose arrest the Sindh CM has ordered — its builder, architect, structural engineer and its contractors have been nominated in the FIR. According to the FIR, the complainant alleged that poor-quality material was being used in the construction of the building. He claimed that the suspects, in collusion with the officials of various government departments, had been involved in constructing additional structures and not complying with the building’s approved plan. This was why the building collapsed around 1pm, the complainant alleged. Police have arrested four of the suspects, including one of the owners, Saad Tahir, and three contractors, who were produced before the judicial magistrate (south) today. The judge granted police a five-day physical remand of the suspects.

items.title: UN refugee agency seeks $7.1 bn in 2027
items.description: The United Nations' refugee agency said on Friday it was seeking a much-reduced $7.1 billion to protect stateless people and respond to emergencies in 2027. UNHCR chief Barham Salih warned last month that his agency was being "asked to do the impossible", over-stretched by a huge funding shortfall and near record-high population displacements around the world. UNHCR's 2026 appeal targeted $8.5 billion -- of which only $2.9 billion has been raised to date.

items.title: The Good Old Days of American Spy Movies and TV
items.description: This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. Spies, at least for now, are back in the public eye: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond—I’ve said all I’ll say on that — and the Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang, confessed to canoodling with an alleged Chinese-intelligence asset, so we’re thinking about espionage again. But after the Cold War, with a few notable exceptions, including the eternal 007 series, the entertainment industry lost interest in spies for the most part. On television, they have reemerged only in occasional treats such as the wonderful Slow Horses , a series about a bunch of dedicated but often incompetent MI5 operatives. And that’s too bad, because the days when spies were everywhere in American culture were a blast. The heyday of pop-spy mania ran from the early 1960s to about the mid-1970s. Some of these offerings are well worth revisiting, not only as entertainment but also as fascinating cultural artifacts of an era when America was leading the free world in the fight against the Kremlin. (Given the current state of U.S. foreign policy , you can imagine why I am nostalgic for such times.) During that spy craze, American culture mostly imported products from the spy-thriller mother country, the United Kingdom. (As early as 1954, CBS ran the first television adaptation of an Ian Fleming novel, a version of Casino Royale that features an American James Bond—named Jimmy Bond, I kid you not—played by Barry Nelson.) But the cultural obsession with spies really took off in the mid-1960s, by which point Sean Connery had established 007 as an international film hero. Why were we so infatuated with espionage during the swingin’ ’60s? The Cold War obviously had a lot to do with it. Americans for the first time faced an enemy superpower, but in the atomic age, when the price of war was too high, they had to fight their opponents in the shadows. This era of spies was also a product of the liberated mores of the times. Movies, especially, were allowed to be racier, and spy flicks soon featured handsome cads cheerfully engaging in plenty of sex and violence. Bond and his colleagues represented a new image of virility and savoir faire, freed from the uptight 1950s. But they also defiantly rejected the more progressive changes of the ’60s. Feminism? Criminal rights? Forget it. These new spies had a license to kill, to use women like toys, to drive like maniacs, to gamble, to drink, and to do anything else a manly man thought was necessary to save the world. British spy shows, more grounded in the reality of European espionage, were generally grittier and less flashy than the Hollywood-ized Bond movies. Some of them, however, were sexed up when exported to more gung-ho U.S. viewers. From 1960 to 1961, for example, Patrick McGoohan played John Drake on Danger Man , an agent who works for some nebulous NATO intelligence agency. As Bond mania grew, the series was revived in 1964, losing some of its film-noir elements in favor of more 007 influences. Drake was moved over to British intelligence, the show was retitled Secret Agent for U.S. syndication, and Johnny Rivers performed a new theme song that became a ’60s classic. After Secret Agent ended its run in late 1967, McGoohan followed it up in 1968 with The Prisoner , a kind of spy-fi (spy-and-science-fiction mash-up) series about an agent who tries to retire and is sent to a secret halfway house for wayward spooks. The series, which is still a cult favorite, calls his character only “Number Six”—but we all knew it was Drake. Likewise, when The Avengers premiered in the U.K. in 1961, it was mostly a pedestrian private-eye show. But soon, it turned into a spy-fi romp, with John Steed (Patrick Macnee) and his female colleague Mrs. Gale (Honor Blackman) as the agents who served Queen and country. In a case of spy-fiction cross-pollination, Blackman left to play Pussy Galore in Goldfinger , the 007 adventure about a plot to blow up America’s gold reserves in Kentucky. After Diana Rigg arrived as Steed’s new partner, Emma Peel, the show winked at the audience: In a 1965 episode, she hands Steed his mail, including a Christmas card from Gale. “How nice of her to remember me,” Steed says. “What can she be doing in Fort Knox?” The next year, the series was snapped up by America’s ABC, and Rigg, in her leather catsuits , and Macnee, in his bowler hat and Pierre Cardin suits, became spy-fiction icons. Spies quickly flooded U.S. television screens after what must have been an endless stream of high-concept pitches: “James Bond, but in the old American West as a Secret Service agent, against supervillains with names such as Dr. Loveless and Count Manzeppi.” ( The Wild Wild West .) “James Bond, but as an incompetent boob in a comedy.” ( Get Smart! ) “James Bond, but he’s a Black American tennis pro.” ( I Spy . The series’ star, Bill Cosby, now lives in shame, but back in 1965, it was groundbreaking to get Americans to accept a Black man as the hero instead of a sidekick.) The Man From U.N.C.L.E. , a show that first hit TV screens in 1964, was spy-fi from the start. Not only was it derived from the Bond successes, but Fleming reportedly helped develop an early pitch for the show; U.N.C.L.E. Agent Napoleon Solo was even named for a Bond character. Solo and his Soviet partner, Ilya Kuriakin, work for U.N.C.L.E., a kind of international superagency that battles the psychos from T.H.R.U.S.H., an obvious stand-in for Fleming’s baddies, SPECTRE. ( U.N.C.L.E. producers came up with these names because they sounded hip; they filled in what the acronyms meant later.) The Americans had their own homegrown spies, too. In 1966, Mission: Impossible premiered on CBS featuring a team of operatives so secret that the U.S. government hides their instructions on a tape recorder in a telephone booth or a vending machine and other wacky places, after which the tape self-destructs into a hissing, smoky mess. (The Tom Cruise Mission: Impossible reboots, much like the Jason Bourne movies, are fine as generic action flicks, but for some Cold War spy fun, treat yourself to the original series.) Even cartoons got in on the act. Everyone remembers Bullwinkle’s enemies, Boris and Natasha, and you might remember Secret Squirrel, but do you remember Cool McCool, a 1966 Saturday-morning secret agent drummed up by Bob Kane, a co-creator of Batman? Probably not, and that’s fine, because Cool McCool is terrible. (But not as terrible as “Lancelot Link, Secret Chimp” a 1970 spy spoof for kids that had a cast of, yes, live chimpanzees.) Eventually, the spy craze got out of hand, as all fads do. James Coburn and Dean Martin both signed up for spy spoofs, and saw varying results: Coburn’s two outings as Derek Flint, an agent of Z.O.W.I.E. (don’t ask), are fine, but Martin’s Matt Helm movies are unwatchable—at least they provided some raw material for Mike Myers when he created Austin Powers . After the 1960s, the cynical ’70s were upon us, and the fascination with spies dissipated. Events such as Watergate made government spookery seem a lot less admirable; in 1975, a congressional committee outed a lot of the CIA’s uglier tricks to the American public. Bond movies thrived, but 007 had much of the spy-genre field to himself at the theaters and on television. It was a great ride, and you can catch many of these programs on stations that run vintage TV shows, random YouTube channels , or a few streaming platforms. That’s your assignment over this holiday weekend, Agent Reader, and remember: This newsletter will self-destruct in five seconds. Related: Sorry, Robert Pattinson is not James Bond. 10 questions to determine whether your partner is a spy, by Alexandra Petri Here are three stories from The Atlantic : David A. Graham’s tumultuous journey across the Atlantic on a wind-powered cargo ship Orwell has become what he despised, Stephen Marche argues. Here comes Santa Claude, Evening Read Black Friday shoppers at a Toys “R” Us in Fort Worth, Texas, in 2009 Tom Pennington / Getty Black Friday Nostalgia ( From 2025 ) By Annie Joy Williams Every Thanksgiving when I was growing up, my family held a Wacky Tacky Talent Show so needlessly competitive that at least one kid inevitably cried. And on the same special tablecloth we used every year, we would list with a felt-tip marker what we were most grateful for: I’d write my dog and American Girl doll; my mother would write me and my sisters; my college-aged cousin would write her boyfriend du jour (there were many crossed-out names on the fabric). Then I would sit down with a pile of buttered mashed potatoes and wait for midnight, when the real holiday would begin, the one that made my mini shopaholic’s heart beam: Black Friday. items.title: Mauvais classement dans l’IPC : l’OFNAC et le Forum Civil passent à l’offensive
items.description: Depuis près de trois décennies, le Sénégal peine à sortir de la zone rouge de l’Indice de perception de la corruption. Face à cette contre-performance persistante, l’OFNAC et le Forum Civil veulent changer de stratégie. Réunis à Saly le 27 et 28 Novembre , les deux acteurs entendent poser les jalons d’une riposte collective, fondée sur l’auto-évaluation, des réformes ciblées et une meilleure implication des institutions, avec un objectif clair : faire passer le Sénégal au-dessus de la barre des 50 %. MBOUR – Améliorer le positionnement du Sénégal dans l’Indice de perception de la corruption (IPC) et lui permettre de sortir de la zone rouge constitue désormais un objectif majeur pour l’OFNAC et le Forum Civil. Depuis 1998, le pays peine à quitter durablement cette catégorie, malgré les différentes initiatives engagées dans le domaine de la lutte contre la corruption.Face à cette situation, les deux organisations ambitionnent de dépasser la simple observation des résultats publiés par Transparency International pour adopter une démarche plus proactive, fondée sur l’auto-évaluation, l’identification des insuffisances et la mise en œuvre de mesures correctives. À l’ouverture de l’atelier, le directeur de l’OFNAC, Moustapha Ka, a mis l’accent sur l’importance d’une mobilisation de toutes les parties prenantes. Selon lui, l’amélioration du score du Sénégal ne saurait être l’œuvre d’une seule institution, mais nécessite une véritable synergie entre les différents acteurs concernés.« Le score qu’on veut atteindre ne dépend pas d’une seule structure. Il faut la conjugaison, en tout cas la cohésion des efforts de tous les acteurs impliqués », a-t-il déclaré. Il estime notamment que l’atteinte du seuil de 50 % permettrait au Sénégal de sortir de la zone rouge.Moustapha Ka a également rappelé que cette rencontre s’inscrit dans le prolongement de la convention de partenariat signée entre l’OFNAC et le Forum Civil. Celle-ci vise notamment à favoriser les échanges d’informations, le partage d’expériences et la diffusion de bonnes pratiques. Pour le directeur de l’OFNAC, il est désormais nécessaire de prendre les devants en matière d’évaluation, au lieu de se limiter à subir les résultats de l’indice. « Il est temps qu’on arrête de subir l’évaluation. Il est temps également que nous fassions les premiers pas pour faire une pré-évaluation, une auto-évaluation, une introspection », a-t-il soutenu. Des études pour identifier les secteurs vulnérables La question des secteurs les plus exposés à la corruption a également été abordée au cours des échanges. Sur ce point, le directeur de l’OFNAC a reconnu qu’il n’existe pas encore de données suffisamment précises pour établir une classification des administrations les plus vulnérables. Il a toutefois rappelé que le phénomène touche l’ensemble des administrations publiques, y compris la justice.« La corruption est présente dans toutes les administrations, y compris la justice et d’autres secteurs », a-t-il affirmé. Dans le but de mieux identifier les risques et les failles susceptibles de favoriser ces pratiques, l’OFNAC a entrepris des études de vulnérabilité dans plusieurs départements ministériels, notamment ceux de l’Environnement, des Transports et de la Justice.Ces études consistent à examiner, en collaboration avec les acteurs concernés, les insuffisances relevées dans les procédures administratives, les pratiques professionnelles et le fonctionnement des différents services. Les résultats attendus devraient permettre d'élaborer des feuilles de route et de concevoir, de manière concertée, des codes déontologiques adaptés aux réalités et aux spécificités de chaque secteur. A lire aussi : Saint-Louis : Le Forum Civil mobilise les acteurs autour des droits numériques De son côté, le coordonnateur général du Forum Civil, Matar Sall, a insisté sur la persistance du mauvais classement du Sénégal dans l’Indice de perception de la corruption. Il a rappelé que, depuis le début de son évaluation en 1998, le pays n’a jamais réussi à sortir durablement de la zone rouge.« Depuis 1998, le Sénégal est évalué et reste toujours dans la zone rouge. Il n'y a pas eu une seule année où le Sénégal est sorti de la zone rouge », a-t-il fait remarquer. Pour Matar Sall, l'atelier constitue une occasion de mieux comprendre les critères et les sources d'évaluation utilisés par Transparency International, mais également d'identifier les leviers susceptibles de contribuer à l'amélioration du score national.Il a, à cet égard, tenu à apporter une précision sur la nature de cet indicateur. L’IPC, a-t-il expliqué, ne repose pas directement sur la perception des citoyens, mais sur des évaluations et des sources spécifiques permettant d'apprécier le niveau de corruption dans les différents pays. Le coordonnateur général du Forum Civil a par ailleurs reconnu que des avancées ont été enregistrées grâce à certaines réformes, tout en estimant que les résultats obtenus demeurent insuffisants au regard des attentes. « Tout ce qui est attendu n’est pas encore fait », a-t-il souligné, appelant ainsi à identifier les mesures supplémentaires à prendre pour améliorer les performances du Sénégal. Ibrahima MBAYE ( Correspondant)

items.title: ‘Not a chance’ – Fulham coach Arbeloa rules out Calvin Bassey sale
items.description: Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa has ruled out the possibility of Nigeria international Calvin Bassey leaving the club during the January transfer window amid reported interest from Manchester United. Arbeloa described the 26-year-old defender as an important member of his squad, insisting that Fulham have no intention of allowing him to leave midway through the season. Manchester United are reportedly among several clubs monitoring Bassey following his impressive performances for the London club. However, speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of Fulham’s meeting with Bournemouth, Arbeloa dismissed suggestions that the Red Devils could secure the defender’s services in January. “I’m so happy with Calvin,” Arbeloa told reporters at his pre-Bournemouth press conference. “Obviously, he’s not on sale. No chance that he can leave this club in January. I think he’s happy here, he’s one of our captains, he’s one of our leaders.” The Fulham manager also highlighted Bassey’s leadership qualities and importance to the team’s defensive setup, suggesting that his contributions extend beyond his performances on the pitch. Rather than being concerned about the reported interest from other clubs, Arbeloa views it as recognition of the defender’s performances and growing importance. Fulham are also understood to be taking steps towards securing Bassey’s long-term future, with discussions over a new contract already underway. The development could further complicate any potential attempt by Manchester United or other interested clubs to sign the Nigerian during the winter transfer window. Bassey has established himself as an important figure at Fulham since joining from Ajax in 2023, bringing defensive versatility, physical strength and experience to the squad. The former Rangers defender has also been a regular member of Nigeria’s national team, featuring prominently for the Super Eagles in international competitions. Don Jazzy’s father releases new single to mark 74th birthday
items.description: Collins Ifeanyi Enebeli Ajereh, father of renowned music producer Don Jazzy, has released a new single titled Steeze With Mavin Grandpa to celebrate his 74th birthday. The veteran artiste manager unveiled the song on Thursday, November 26, 2026, alongside plans to release 200 episodes of a reality show bearing the same title. Popularly known as Mavin Grandpa Worldwide (MGW), Ajereh also announced plans to release a music video for the single, which was filmed at selected locations in Europe and Nigeria. The song features Azeena and Naffy, artistes signed to Peachrose label, in what the septuagenarian described as a creative project aimed at connecting with different generations. The planned reality series will offer viewers a glimpse into his personal life, career journey and everyday activities, tracing his experiences across different aspects of the entertainment industry. Ajereh has built a career spanning music, acting, record label ownership and artiste management. He is also known for his academic work on Afrobeat. He is the president and co-founder of the Artiste Managers Association in Nigeria (AMAN), which marked its 30th anniversary with a major entertainment event attended by artistes, managers and other industry stakeholders. The birthday release adds to his activities in the entertainment industry as he continues to explore music and screen productions. items.title: L’UE mobilise un million d’euros pour l’aide humanitaire au nord du Togo et du Bénin
items.description: Lomé, 27 nov. (ATOP) – L’Union européenne (UE) a mobilisé un financement supplémentaire d’un million d’euros pour soutenir les populations vulnérables touchées par les conflits, les déplacements et l’insécurité alimentaire dans le nord du Togo et du Bénin. Cette enveloppe fait partie d’un financement additionnel de 39,5 millions d’euros destiné à répondre aux besoins humanitaires les plus urgents dans les régions du Sahel et du bassin du lac Tchad. L’annonce a été faite le jeudi 12 novembre par la commissaire européenne à l’Égalité, à la préparation et à la gestion des crises, Hadja Lahbib, lors d’une réunion des hauts fonctionnaires consacrée à la situation humanitaire dans ces régions. Ce financement s’inscrit dans le cadre du paquet d’aide humanitaire annoncé par l’UE lors de la dernière Assemblée générale des Nations unies. Avec cette enveloppe supplémentaire, le financement humanitaire total de l’UE pour le Sahel et le bassin du lac Tchad atteint 263,5 millions d’euros en 2026. Au nord du Togo et du Bénin, cette aide permettra de fournir des transferts monétaires polyvalents aux populations déplacées, de renforcer la préparation aux catastrophes et d’améliorer les services de protection, de santé et de nutrition. Dans l’ensemble des régions du Sahel et du lac Tchad, le financement européen aide les partenaires humanitaires à apporter une assistance d’urgence aux populations dans le besoin. Les interventions concernent notamment l’alimentation, la nutrition, les soins de santé, la protection, l’accès à l’eau et à l’assainissement ainsi que l’éducation en situation d’urgence. Les actions sont adaptées aux besoins propres à chaque pays. L’Union européenne précise que son aide humanitaire est accordée sur la base des besoins, dans le respect des principes humanitaires. Elle appelle également au respect du droit international humanitaire et à la protection des populations civiles ainsi que des travailleurs humanitaires. ATOP/AO (Source : Communiqué de presse de la Délégation de l’Union européenne auprès de la République togolaise)

items.title: Forum cybersécurité Gabon 2026 : à l’Aninf, le pari de la souveraineté numérique
items.description: Forum cybersécurité Gabon 2026 : à l’Aninf, le pari de la souveraineté numérique À l’heure où la transformation numérique expose davantage les États, les entreprises et les citoyens aux cybermenaces, la maîtrise des données et la sécurisation des infrastructures deviennent des impératifs de souveraineté. Autour de ces défis que s’est ouverte, le 27 novembre à Libreville, la troisième édition du Forum cybersécurité Gabon 2026, organisée par l’Agence nationale des infrastructures numériques et des fréquences (Aninf), ST Digital et CNConsulting. Quelque 400 participants prennent part à cette rencontre placée sous le thème «Souveraineté numérique, intelligence artificielle et cybersécurité : bâtir un écosystème numérique de confiance pour le Gabon et la sous-région». Les membres du premier panel du forum s’exprimant sur la «Coopération régionale et écosystème de confiance». © GabonReview La troisième édition du forum Cybersécurité Gabon 2026 s’est ouverte ce vendredi 27 novembre, à Libreville, à la Tour Aninf, sous le thème « Souveraineté numérique, intelligence artificielle et cybersécurité : bâtir un écosystème numérique de confiance pour le Gabon et la sous-région ». Portée par l’Agence nationale des infrastructures numériques et des fréquences (Aninf), ST Digital et CNConsulting, la rencontre réunit décideurs publics, dirigeants d’entreprises, les directeurs des systèmes informatiques (DSI), les Responsables de la sécurité des systèmes d'information (RSSI), les experts, les partenaires technologiques et représentants diplomatiques. Son ambition est de faire de la cybersécurité non plus une préoccupation technique, mais une condition de souveraineté, de résilience économique et de confiance numérique. Renforcer les capacités nationales, promouvoir l’hébergement local des données À l’ouverture des travaux, le directeur général de l’Aninf, Alberto Wenceslas Mounguengui Moudoki, a appelé à une mobilisation collective associant pouvoirs publics et secteur privé. « Lorsque nous travaillons la main dans la main, lorsque nous comprenons les enjeux des mêmes écosystèmes, nous nous mettons ensemble pour réfléchir », a-t-il fait savoir. Une approche qui traduit l’ambition du forum à savoir de renforcer les capacités nationales, promouvoir l’hébergement local des données et de favoriser les partenariats technologiques. La directrice générale de ST Digital, Laïka Mba, a, pour sa part, insisté sur la portée de ce rendez-vous. « Aujourd'hui, cette troisième édition est devenue un rendez-vous incontournable pour tous les Gabonais qui sont dans la « tech » mais qui travaillent également dans les métiers de la cybersécurité », a-t-il déclaré. Clichés du forum sur la Cybersécurité Gabon 2026, à Libreville, le 27 novembre 2026. © GabonReview La leçon inaugurale, prononcée par l’ambassadeur Noël Nelson Messone, Ambassadeur, ancien ministre des Nouvelles technologies, sur les enjeux diplomatiques de la cybersécurité en Afrique, a donné une dimension géopolitique aux échanges. Il s’est appesanti sur le thème « les enjeux diplomatique de la cybersécurité pour l’Afrique ». De son exposé, on apprend qu’en 2025, « les dix pays africains les plus ciblés ont enregistré 240 901 477 attaques et tentatives d’attaques ». Le premier pays concerné en a recensé plus de 93 millions. Pour le diplomate, « la cybersécurité n'est plus simplement une question technique. Elle est entrée dans les préoccupations politiques, diplomatiques et géopolitiques ». «L'Afrique ne peut pas attendre d'avoir tous les moyens technologiques pour agir» Souveraineté des données, intelligence artificielle, cloud africain, protection des infrastructures critiques et lutte contre la cybercriminalité structurent également les discussions. Laïka Mba a rappelé que « le secteur public est en train de prendre le train en marche », alors que des infrastructures nationales permettent déjà l’hébergement des données, au Gabon. La rencontre réunit notamment des experts internationaux, dont des représentants d'une association africaine de cybersécurité comptant 37 pays membres. on note particulièrement la présence du Dr Divine Selassié Agbeti, le directeur général de la Cyber ​​security authority (CSA) du Ghana, président du Réseau africain des autorités de cybersécurité (ANCA). Par-delà les échanges techniques, les participants envisage de transformer les contributions en réponses tangibles. Une feuille de route destinée aux autorités compétentes doit notamment prolonger les travaux. Pour Noël Nelson Messone, « l'Afrique ne peut pas attendre d'avoir tous les moyens technologiques pour agir ». Formation, harmonisation des législations, partage de renseignements et coopération régionale constituent ainsi les éléments d'une résilience durable face aux menaces numériques. items.title: The future of food security will be shaped in countries: Why Accra matters – FAO Deputy DG
items.description: In December, Accra will become a global meeting point for a conversation that concerns every country and every family: how can we build agrifood systems capable of feeding people in a world of increasing uncertainty? From 7 to 10 December, Ghana will host the Fourth Global Working Conference of FAO Representatives, bringing together FAO’s leadership on the ground from across the world. The choice of Accra is significant. Africa is central not only to the global food security challenge, but also to many of the solutions we urgently need. We meet at a time of both progress and profound pressure. Around 645 million people faced hunger in 2025, while 2.7 billion people could not afford a healthy diet. At the same time, nearly 300 million people face high levels of acute food insecurity, with conflict, extreme weather and economic shocks increasingly reinforcing one another. These figures tell us something important. Food security today is not simply about producing more food. It is about access, affordability and nutrition. It is about resilience to climate and economic shocks. And it is about creating opportunities and livelihoods, particularly for rural communities. For Africa, the stakes are especially high. The continent has enormous agricultural potential, abundant innovation and the world’s youngest population. But it also faces growing climate pressures, conflict and economic vulnerabilities. This is why our message in Accra must be clear: the world does not need more diagnosis alone. It needs faster translation of knowledge into country-level results. The conference will focus on four shifts that can help us achieve this. First, from response to anticipation. Too often, the international community intervenes only after droughts, floods or other shocks have destroyed crops, livestock and livelihoods. Today, better information, early-warning systems and anticipatory action allow us to act earlier. We can identify risks, establish triggers and protect people’s productive assets before a shock becomes a humanitarian crisis. Second, from projects to systems. Individual projects matter, but lasting transformation requires more: effective policies, stronger institutions, infrastructure, investment and viable markets. FAO must help countries connect technical knowledge with national priorities and bring successful solutions to scale. Third, from funding to financing. Traditional development assistance alone will not provide the resources required to transform agrifood systems. Public resources remain essential, but we must use them more strategically to mobilize climate finance, development finance and responsible private investment. We need to turn good ideas into bankable investment opportunities that strengthen local value chains and create opportunities for farmers, entrepreneurs, women and young people. Fourth, from digital tools to digital public value. Artificial intelligence, digital agriculture and better data can transform access to information, finance, markets and services. But technology is not an end in itself. Our real measure of success must be whether innovation improves people’s lives and reaches small-scale producers and vulnerable communities. These shifts point towards a broader change in the way international organizations operate. FAO’s country offices must increasingly become platforms for impact: bringing together governments, the UN system, financial institutions, the private sector and communities; connecting knowledge with investment; and transforming global expertise into measurable national results. This is particularly relevant for Africa. Africa must not be seen simply as a continent where the world’s food security challenges need to be addressed. It must increasingly be recognized as a continent where solutions are being created and where investment in agrifood systems can generate wider economic and social transformation. Hosting this conference gives Ghana an opportunity to help shape that global conversation. By the end of our work in Accra, we should be able to answer three practical questions: What must we scale? What must we fix? What must we do differently. The answers will matter far beyond FAO. They will determine whether early warnings reach farmers before crops are lost; whether young entrepreneurs can turn innovation into viable businesses; whether investment strengthens local value chains; and whether international cooperation builds lasting capabilities in countries. That is the ambition we should bring to Accra: to act earlier, invest better, scale what works and deliver greater impact where it matters most, in countries and communities. The future of food security will ultimately be shaped on the ground. And Africa must be at the centre of shaping that future. By Maurizio Martina, FAO Deputy Director-General, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

items.title: ¿Ser propietario o inquilino influye en el voto? Lo que revela un estudio con más de 80 elecciones
items.description: Imaginemos una situación hipotética: dos españoles de 40 años salen a votar . Ambos viven en la misma ciudad, que podría ser Madrid, Barcelona, Teruel o Soria. Tienen el mismo nivel de estudios, el mismo tipo de trabajo y el mismo sueldo. Solo hay una diferencia: uno es propietario y el otro vive de alquiler. Ese detalle pesa hoy más en su papeleta que su propio empleo, según un estudio publicado en la revista Electoral Studies que analiza más de 80 elecciones en 14 democracias occidentales avanzadas —entre ellas España— desde 1985. items.title: Coopération militaire : le Maroc et Israël tiennent leur quatrième réunion de la commission mixte à Rabat
items.description: La quatrième réunion de la commission militaire mixte maroco-israélienne s’est achevée jeudi 26 novembre 2026 au siège de l’État-major général des Forces armées royales (FAR), à Rabat. Les travaux ont notamment permis de dresser le bilan de la coopération militaire entre les deux pays en 2026 et de définir les perspectives pour 2027. À l’issue de cette rencontre, les deux parties ont procédé à la signature du procès-verbal de la réunion, qui a également été l’occasion de convenir d’un plan d’action commun pour l’année 2027. Les deux délégations ont, par ailleurs, réaffirmé leur engagement à renforcer la coopération militaire bilatérale et à soutenir les efforts conjoints en vue d’atteindre les objectifs fixés. Enfin, les deux parties ont convenu de tenir la cinquième réunion de la commission militaire mixte maroco-israélienne en Israël, en 2027. The post Coopération militaire : le Maroc et Israël tiennent leur quatrième réunion de la commission mixte à Rabat appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Renouvellement des CNI : la DAF étend l’opération aux cartes délivrées jusqu’en janvier 2017
items.description: La Direction de l’automatisation des fichiers (DAF) élargit le dispositif de renouvellement des cartes nationales d’identité biométriques CEDEAO arrivant à expiration. À compter du 3 décembre 2026, l’opération concernera également les cartes délivrées jusqu’au 31 janvier 2017. Les titulaires concernés sont invités à se rapprocher des centres d’enrôlement pour effectuer leur demande. La mesure s’étend à une nouvelle catégorie de détenteurs de cartes nationales d’identité (CNI). Dans un communiqué rendu public le 27 novembre 2026, la Direction de l’automatisation des fichiers (DAF), relevant du ministère de l’Intérieur et de la Sécurité publique, annonce que le renouvellement des cartes nationales d’identité biométriques CEDEAO arrivant à expiration sera étendu, à partir du 3 décembre prochain, aux cartes délivrées au mois de janvier 2017. Sont ainsi concernés les titulaires de CNI délivrées entre le 4 octobre 2016 et le 31 janvier 2017. La DAF les invite à se rendre dans les centres d’enrôlement pour introduire leur demande de renouvellement. Au Sénégal, les démarches peuvent être effectuées auprès des commissariats de police, des préfectures et des sous-préfectures. À l’étranger, les ressortissants concernés peuvent s’adresser aux ambassades et aux consulats. La Direction de l’automatisation des fichiers exhorte les citoyens concernés à entreprendre les démarches le plus tôt possible afin de procéder au renouvellement de leurs titres d’identité. Cette extension du dispositif vise à prendre en compte les cartes délivrées durant la période indiquée et arrivant à expiration. C.G.D

items.title: Toronto’s crime concerns resurface; police seize loaded Glock, drugs in Jane–St. Clair investigation
items.description: Toronto Police have arrested two people after seizing a loaded handgun, ammunition, several suspected illicit drugs and cash during a drug trafficking investigation in the Jane Street and St. Clair Avenue West area. According to a police statement issued on Thursday, November 26, 2026, officers from the 14 Division Major Crime Unit began investigating suspected drug trafficking in the area in October. On November 23, investigators executed a search warrant under the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act at a residence in the neighbourhood. The search reportedly led to the seizure of a loaded Glock 33 subcompact semi-automatic handgun, a firearm magazine containing eight rounds of ammunition, and quantities of cocaine, fentanyl, crystal methamphetamine, heroin and marijuana. Police also seized a large amount of cash. Two Toronto residents were arrested in connection with the investigation. Flavio Cinelli, 47, faces several charges, including six counts of possession of a Schedule I substance for the purpose of trafficking, possession for the purpose of selling, possession of proceeds of crime exceeding $5,000, firearm-related offences and driving while suspended. Lucy Gallo, 50, was also charged with several offences, including drug-related offences, possession of a loaded regulated firearm and driving while suspended. Both accused were scheduled to appear at the Toronto Regional Bail Centre at 2201 Finch Avenue West on November 25, 2026. The charges have not been proven in court, and both accused are presumed innocent unless proven guilty. Police seek public assistance The investigation highlights continuing concerns about the presence of illegal firearms and drug trafficking in residential neighbourhoods. The combination of a loaded handgun, ammunition and multiple suspected illicit substances seized during the operation has also drawn attention to the potential public safety risks associated with drug-related criminal activity. Toronto Police say public cooperation remains important in identifying suspects, gathering evidence and preventing further criminal activity. Anyone with information about the investigation is urged to contact 14 Division at 416-808-1400. The police operation forms part of ongoing efforts to address drug-related offences and illegal firearm possession across Toronto, with authorities relying on investigations and community cooperation to improve neighbourhood safety.

items.title: Grève du SNESUP, les parents d’élèves appellent au dialogue
items.description: Depuis plus d'un mois, les enseignants-chercheurs observent un mouvement de greve pour reclamer le paiement de la prime de recherche. Alors qu'aucun compromis n'a encore ete trouve entre le syndicat et le gouvernement, la situation preoccupe la Federation nationale des associations des parents d'eleves et etudiants du Mali FENAPEM. L'organisation appelle les deux parties a privilegier le dialogue afin de parvenir rapidement a une issue a la crise. Pour la FENAPEM, cette situation ne profite a aucune des parties concernees. Elle estime que la poursuite de la greve risque de penaliser aussi bien les enseignants que les etudiants et leurs familles, sans oublier l'etat. Daouda Sacko, secretaire general adjoint de la FENAPEM, plaide pour un reglement a l'amiable du differend . Il invite le syndicat et le gouvernement a se retrouver autour de la table des negociations pour parvenir a un compromis acceptable. Le dialogue comme solution « C'est une situation qui n'arrange personne, ni les professeurs, ni les etudiants, ni les parents d'etudiants, ni l'etat. Donc, il faut le dialogue », souligne Daouda Sacko. Il souhaite egalement que les deux parties fassent preuve de bon sens et de comprehension afin de trouver un terrain d'entente. « Il faut que les deux parties arrivent a une bonne comprehension de la situation et fassent des propositions acceptables, valables et durables », preconise-t-il. Face a l'impasse des negociations, la FENAPEM espere ainsi une reprise du dialogue entre le gouvernement et les enseignants-chercheurs pour eviter une prolongation de la crise dans les universites. items.title: Battling Siki: Saint-Louis prépare le centenaire de son assassinat
items.description: A l’approche du centenaire de l’assassinat d’Amadou Louis Mbarick Fall, dit Battling Siki, Saint-Louis prépare quatre jours de commémoration, du 12 au 15 décembre 2026. Un comité départemental de développement tenu jeudi à la gouvernance, a permis de faire le point sur l’organisation des activités dédiées à ce champion du monde de boxe et héros de guerre. La rencontre s’est déroulée sous la présidence de l’adjoint au préfet de Saint-Louis, Abdou Khadre Dieylani Ba, représentant le gouverneur Al Hassan Sall. Les services techniques présents ont manifesté leur disponibilité à accompagner le comité d’organisation. « Nous saluons les efforts fournis par le comité d’organisation pour la tenue de ce centenaire », a déclaré Abdou Khadre Dieylani Ba, réaffirmant l’engagement de l’administration territoriale à contribuer à la réussite de l’événement. Pour Marième Fall Soda, présidente de l’Association pour la mémoire d’Amadou Mbarick Fall et petite-fille du champion, cette commémoration dépasse le cadre familial. Elle rappelle le parcours d’un homme qui s’est engagé volontairement dans la guerre, a été décoré de la Croix de guerre et de la médaille militaire, avant de devenir champion du monde de boxe en 1922. « Battling, c’est un héros de guerre, un champion du monde et l’un des plus grands patrimoines historiques de l’État », a-t-elle souligné, invitant les populations à participer aux activités. Le programme débutera le 12 décembre par une soirée culturelle. Le 13 décembre, la cérémonie officielle sera suivie d’un gala international de boxe. Le 14 décembre, un colloque portera sur la vie et l’œuvre de Battling Siki, avec la présentation et la dédicace du livre de Marième Fall Soda consacré à son parcours. La journée du 15 décembre, date de la commémoration de son assassinat, sera consacrée au recueillement sur sa tombe au cimetière de Thiaka Ndiaye, à des lectures du Coran et à une conférence religieuse en wolof. A travers cette initiative, les organisateurs entendent faire connaître davantage l’histoire de Battling Siki et transmettre son héritage aux générations futures. Jeanne SAGNA (Correspondante)

items.title: Toronto residents warned of scammers posing as CRA and Shanghai police officers
items.description: Toronto Police are warning residents about a phone scam in which fraudsters allegedly impersonate Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) officials and Shanghai Police officers to obtain sensitive personal and banking information. In a public advisory issued on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, the Toronto Police Service said it had received reports of fraudulent calls in which unsuspecting residents were falsely told they were under investigation for criminal activity in China. According to investigators, the scam typically begins with a caller claiming to represent the CRA. The recipient is then transferred to another individual who identifies himself as a member of the Shanghai Police. The second caller reportedly provides a false name and badge number before claiming to be investigating the recipient’s alleged involvement in criminal activity in China. The caller then requests the person’s banking information, supposedly to prevent or resolve the alleged investigation. Police say these requests are not legitimate investigative procedures but attempts to obtain confidential personal and financial information for fraudulent purposes. A scam built on fear and false authority The reported scheme exploits public trust in government institutions and law enforcement agencies by creating an impression of authority and urgency. By invoking the names of the CRA and a foreign police service, the scammers allegedly put recipients under pressure to disclose information they would otherwise protect. The transfer from one supposed official to another may also make the call appear more credible. Toronto Police are therefore urging residents not to accept a caller’s claimed title, name or badge number as proof of identity. Anyone receiving a call from someone claiming to be a police officer is advised to request the person’s name, badge number and police service, end the call and independently contact the relevant police service using its officially published telephone number. Never disclose banking information over the phone Police are also reminding residents not to share personal, banking or financial information with unknown callers. The Toronto Police Service specifically emphasised that its officers will never request personal banking information over the phone. Such requests should be treated as potential attempts at fraud. Residents are urged to be particularly cautious when unsolicited callers threaten criminal charges, claim that an investigation is underway or demand immediate action. Rather than complying with instructions from an unexpected caller, residents should independently verify the claims through official channels. How to protect yourself Although the police advisory did not provide details of the number of victims, financial losses or arrests linked to the reported scheme, it highlights the need for caution when dealing with unsolicited calls involving alleged criminal investigations. Residents who receive suspicious calls or believe they have been targeted are encouraged to report the matter to the police. Anyone with information about the reported scam can contact Toronto Police investigators on 416-808-5200. The warning serves as a reminder that an official-sounding voice does not necessarily represent a legitimate authority. When someone claiming to be a government official or police officer requests confidential banking information, residents should end the conversation and verify the caller’s identity independently

items.title: L’étoile filante
items.description: Une étoile de champion est censée briller pour l’éternité. Elle symbolise une victoire, un mérite, une consécration qui traversent le temps. Mais l’étoile offerte par la Caf au Maroc, pourtant battu devant son public à Rabat, avait visiblement une autre idée de l’éternité. Dix petits mois de lumière et puis s’en va ! Une véritable étoile filante ! À peine le temps de l’admirer, de la célébrer et de l’accrocher au palmarès, qu’elle reprend déjà la route du Sénégal. Même les étoiles de Noël restent plus longtemps en vitrine ! Pendant que certains savouraient une gloire usurpée, qu’ils croyaient gravée dans le marbre, le Sénégal attendait tranquillement que l’histoire reprenne ses droits. Le peuple, après avoir jubilé, a patienté, en bon propriétaire qui sait que son bien finira par rentrer à la maison. Car un titre gagné sur le terrain n’a pas besoin de rustines pour exister. Il se mérite sur la pelouse, pas dans les couloirs. Cette fois, le Tribunal arbitral du sport a tranché et la Caf n’y peut plus rien. Plus de communiqué, plus de rectificatif, plus de bricolage de dernière minute. Certaines étoiles ne sont que de passage, le temps d’une erreur de trajectoire. La nôtre, elle, est de retour au Sénégal. Et pour de bon ! samba.oumar.fall@lesoleil.sn

Mort d’un inspecteur de police écrasé par une voiture à Oued Zem : deux frères arrêtés
items.description: Les éléments de la Brigade nationale de la police judiciaire (BNPJ), en coordination avec les services de la Direction générale de la surveillance du territoire (DGST), ont procédé ce vendredi à l’arrestation de deux frères soupçonnés d’être impliqués dans le meurtre d’un inspecteur de police, tué après avoir été percuté par une voiture à Oued Zem. Selon une source sécuritaire, les deux suspects faisaient l’objet de plusieurs avis de recherche à l’échelle nationale pour des affaires liées au trafic de drogues dures et à l’agression d’un fonctionnaire public dans l’exercice de ses fonctions. La même source précise que l’inspecteur de police, relevant du commissariat régional de sûreté d’Oued Zem, avait subi de graves blessures et fractures qui ont entraîné son décès lors d’une intervention visant à interpeller les deux individus. Les investigations et les recherches menées par les services de sécurité ont permis de localiser la cachette des suspects et de procéder à leur arrestation. Ils ont été placés en garde à vue dans le cadre de l’enquête judiciaire menée sous la supervision du parquet compétent. À la suite du décès de l’inspecteur, le directeur général de la sûreté nationale et de la surveillance du territoire avait décidé de lui accorder une promotion exceptionnelle. Il avait également chargé les services centraux et sociaux de la Sûreté nationale de présenter leurs condoléances à sa famille, de prendre en charge l’ensemble des frais de ses obsèques et de lui apporter les aides et le soutien financier nécessaires. The post Mort d’un inspecteur de police écrasé par une voiture à Oued Zem : deux frères arrêtés appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Relance des activités de la Mine de Perkouan : Un acte de souveraineté, un engagement à promouvoir le développement endogène
items.description: Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ a présidé ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026, la cérémonie de relance des activités de la mine polymétallique de Perkouan dans la commune de Réo, province du Sanguié, région du Nando. Les activités de la mine de Perkoaun ont repris. Les machines vrombissent et les travailleurs sont à l’ouvrage, en présence du Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, qui a procédé à la visite des installations après le dévoilement de la plaque inaugurale et la coupure du ruban. À travers la relance de cette activité, le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ réaffirme sa vision souverainiste. « On ne peut continuer à laisser brader nos ressources, que tout sorte et qu’on nous serve des miettes. Aujourd’hui nous reprenons le contrôle de notre sous-sol », a-t-il souligné. Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ : « On ne peut continuer à laisser brader nos ressources (…) Aujourd’hui nous reprenons le contrôle de notre sous-sol » « Notre énergie c’est la souveraineté. Quand vous voyez l’histoire de cette mine, après quatre années de pause, elle a été entièrement réhabilitée par des ingénieurs burkinabè. Cela veut dire que nous avons la connaissance, nous avons la capacité. Cette mine appartient à 100% à l’État », a expliqué le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ. Le Ministre de l’Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, Camarade Yacouba Zabré GOUBA au nom du Président du Faso, a rendu un hommage aux travailleurs disparus lors de l’inondation de 2022 « Le Burkina est l’un des rares pays, sinon le seul pays en Afrique à avoir autant de mines industrielles qui lui appartiennent à 100%. Lorsqu’on pense à cette souveraineté, ça ne peut qu’être votre carburant pour évoluer dans cette lutte », a précisé le Président du Faso. Le Directeur général de la SOPAMIB, Ministre Conseil spécial du Président du Faso, Dr Lamissa BARRO a précisé que la production prévisionnelle est de 576 000 tonnes de concentré polymétallique La présence du Chef de l’État en personne pour la remise en fonction de cette unité d’exploitation minière témoigne de son engagement personnel pour l’exploitation endogène de nos ressources naturelles. Elle marque également un tournant très important pour le secteur minier dans la région. Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso

items.title: Violences faites aux femmes : Moussa Sarr annonce une réponse pénale plus ferme
items.description: À l’occasion des 16 jours d’activisme contre les violences faites aux femmes et aux filles, le garde des Sceaux, ministre de la Justice, Me Moussa Sarr, appelle à une mobilisation collective et à une prise en charge judiciaire systématique des signalements. La prochaine circulaire générale de politique pénale donnera des instructions aux parquets pour faire de ces violences une priorité dès le premier signalement. « Aucune violence n'est tolérable dans la République, en particulier celle faite aux femmes. » Cette déclaration du président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, le 31 décembre 2025, doit, selon le garde des Sceaux, se traduire par une action résolue contre toutes les formes de violences faites aux femmes et aux filles. Dans son plaidoyer à l'occasion des 16 jours d'activisme, Me Moussa Sarr dénonce avec fermeté des actes qu'il juge « inacceptables », sans aucune circonstance pouvant les justifier. Le ministre de la Justice attire particulièrement l'attention sur les violences commises dans le cercle familial. Plusieurs femmes ont perdu la vie depuis le début de l'année, souvent sous les coups d'un conjoint ou d'un proche. Pour lui, ces drames ne surviennent pas toujours sans signes précurseurs. Les menaces, les plaintes retirées sous la pression de l'entourage ou le silence face aux premières violences peuvent contribuer à rendre possible le passage à l'acte. Faire du premier signalement une priorité Face à cette réalité, le garde des Sceaux entend renforcer la réponse judiciaire. Il indique que la prochaine circulaire générale de politique pénale, actuellement en cours de finalisation et destinée aux parquets, leur demandera de traiter les violences faites aux femmes comme une priorité dès le premier signalement. L'objectif est de ne laisser aucune alerte sans suite. Me Moussa Sarr adresse ainsi un message aux femmes confrontées à la violence : elles doivent pouvoir parler et être entendues. À l'endroit des auteurs, le ministre est tout aussi ferme : « Ceux qui violentent n'ont rien à attendre de la justice, sinon la rigueur de la loi. » Briser le silence et la banalisation Au-delà de l'action des juridictions, le ministre insiste sur la responsabilité de l'ensemble de la société. Il invite les familles à ne plus considérer les violences faites aux femmes comme des affaires privées, encore moins comme de simples « drames passionnels ». Il appelle également les médias à jouer pleinement leur rôle dans l'éveil des consciences et la sensibilisation de l'opinion. Pour Me Moussa Sarr, la lutte contre ces violences ne saurait reposer sur la seule réponse judiciaire. Elle suppose aussi de rompre avec le silence, les pressions familiales et les justifications coutumières qui peuvent entourer ces actes. L'exigence de protection rappelée par le chef de l'État engage ainsi chaque citoyen. À travers ce plaidoyer, le garde des Sceaux réaffirme la nécessité de construire une société où aucune femme ne doit subir de violences sans que les mécanismes de protection et de justice soient mobilisés. C.G. DIOP

items.title: NDC plans free education, school meals, maternal care in Lagos – Animashaun
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) deputy governorship candidate Moriam Tolani Animashaun says an NDC-led government in Lagos would provide free education and maternal healthcare, including delivery and emergency services. Animashaun spoke at the Road to Election 2027 Lagos Deputy Governorship Debate on Nigeria Info FM on Friday, saying the party’s health and education programmes would be funded by increasing their share of the state budget from 15 to 20 per cent, without imposing additional taxes. “First of all, to make it completely free for mothers and children up to age 60,” she said. “When we say completely, the hope is that they can actually not only the delivery, it’s if there’s any emergency to be able to get to the health, which is why the healthcare centre is really pivotal.” Animashaun said the party planned to establish at least four primary healthcare centres in each of Lagos State’s 20 local government areas. “Ambulances and emergency referrals will all be part of each of those healthcare centres as well,” she said, adding that the facilities would help reduce pressure on general hospitals. On education, she said the proposal would cover school fees, levies, books and at least one meal a day. “When we’re talking about free, we will launch a totally free education, as in no paying for the books. You get two books free at the moment, in the public school. Now we will have a total, all the books will be given free. The fees will be totally free, no tax levy, and at least one meal a day,” she said. Animashaun said the budget allocation for health and education would increase from 15 to 20 per cent “not through any extra levy or any extra taxes.” The deputy governorship candidate, however said she was unsure of the state’s maternal death rate and did not want to provide a figure. Other major contenders at the debate included ADC deputy governorship candidate Babatunde Olalere Gbadamosi and SDP deputy candidate Evelyn Aderiyike Kayode. The debate was hosted by Kofi Bartels and Ireti Bakare-Yusuf. The post NDC plans free education, school meals, maternal care in Lagos – Animashaun appeared first on Vanguard News .

Meet Ime Udoka, Nigerian-American coach leading Houston Rockets in the NBA
items.description: Nigerian-American basketball coach Ime Udoka has built an impressive career in basketball, rising from representing Nigeria on the international stage to coaching some of the biggest teams in the National Basketball Association (NBA). Udoka, who currently serves as head coach of the Houston Rockets, has established himself as one of the prominent coaching figures in American basketball, with a career shaped by years of playing, coaching and leadership experience. Born on August 9, 1977, in Portland, Oregon, United States, Udoka has Nigerian roots and represented Nigeria in international basketball competitions before transitioning into coaching. His playing career included spells in the NBA, the NBA Development League and professional basketball leagues in Europe. He also played for Nigeria at the 2005 and 2011 FIBA AfroBasket tournaments, helping raise the country’s profile in international basketball. After retiring from professional basketball, Udoka moved into coaching, beginning his NBA coaching career as an assistant with the San Antonio Spurs in 2012. He worked under legendary coach Gregg Popovich, gaining experience in player development, team management and tactical preparation. During his time with San Antonio, the Spurs reached the NBA Finals in 2013 and won the championship in 2014, providing Udoka with valuable experience at the highest level of the sport. He subsequently served as an assistant coach with the Philadelphia 76ers and Brooklyn Nets before joining the Boston Celtics in 2021. Led Boston Celtics to NBA Finals Udoka’s breakthrough as a head coach came in 2021 when he was appointed to lead the Boston Celtics. In his first season, he guided the team to the 2022 NBA Finals, where they faced the Golden State Warriors. Although Boston lost the series 4-2, Udoka earned recognition for transforming the team’s defensive performance and guiding its players through a successful playoff campaign. His achievement made him one of the few coaches to reach the NBA Finals in his first season as a head coach. However, his tenure in Boston ended in September 2022 when the franchise suspended him for the 2022–23 season over violations of team policies. New chapter with Houston Rockets In April 2023, the Houston Rockets appointed Udoka as their head coach, giving him another opportunity to lead an NBA franchise. He took charge of a rebuilding team that had struggled in previous seasons and was tasked with improving its competitiveness through tactical discipline, player development and stronger defensive organisation. His appointment marked another significant milestone in his coaching career, as he became responsible for developing a young Houston squad and guiding the franchise towards sustained success. Udoka’s coaching approach has been associated with defensive intensity, accountability and high expectations for players. A Nigerian connection in American basketball Beyond his achievements in the NBA, Udoka’s career also represents a connection between Nigerian basketball and the American professional game. His decision to represent Nigeria internationally highlighted his Nigerian heritage and provided an example of the contribution of players of Nigerian descent to the development of basketball beyond the country. From wearing Nigeria’s colours on the court to leading an NBA team from the sidelines, Udoka’s journey reflects the opportunities that can emerge through talent, experience and determination. His rise from international basketball player to NBA head coach has made him a notable Nigerian-American figure in global sport. The post Meet Ime Udoka, Nigerian-American coach leading Houston Rockets in the NBA appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Trafic de drogue à Conakry : la Police interpelle 29 personnes à Sonfonia
items.description: La Police nationale a interpellé 29 personnes, dont six femmes, lors d’une vaste opération antidrogue menée ce jeudi 26 novembre 2026 dans la commune de Sonfonia, à Conakry. Plusieurs substances présumées stupéfiantes ont également été saisies. Dénommée « Ouragan », cette opération de ratissage a mobilisé des unités de la CMIS, de la BAC et de la BSIP de Sonfonia. Elle s’inscrit dans le cadre des actions engagées par la Police nationale pour lutter contre le trafic et la consommation de stupéfiants dans la capitale et ses environs. Au cours de cette intervention, les agents ont saisi plusieurs produits, notamment du chanvre indien, du haschich ainsi que des comprimés de tramadol. Les 29 personnes interpellées ont été conduites au Commissariat central de Sonfonia pour les besoins de l’enquête et de la procédure judiciaire. À travers cette opération, la Police nationale réaffirme sa volonté de renforcer la lutte contre les stupéfiants et de préserver la sécurité publique. Elle invite par ailleurs les citoyens à signaler toute activité suspecte en appelant le numéro vert 117.
