items.title: FG launches scheme to give 600 Nigerian tailors ₦5m each – How to apply
items.description: The Federal Government has introduced a business support programme to empower 600 tailors across Nigeria, with each selected beneficiary expected to receive ₦5 million in grants and repayable business financing. The initiative, known as the Business Incubation for Renewed Hope Tailors Programme, will run for five years and is being implemented through the Industrial Training Fund (ITF). The programme is designed to help skilled artisans establish, strengthen and expand their tailoring businesses, while creating employment opportunities across the country. The ITF announced the initiative during a pre-launch sensitisation exercise in Jos, Plateau State, where it disclosed that 150 tailors from the North-Central zone had been selected for the pilot phase. The initiative is one of the exit pathways under the ITF’s Skill-Up Artisans Programme (SUPA), which seeks to improve the technical and business skills of Nigerian artisans. Who is eligible for the programme? The programme is open to both participants of the ITF’s Skill-Up Artisans Programme and tailors who received their training outside the scheme. However, prospective beneficiaries must meet specific requirements to qualify. How can interested tailors apply? The ITF has not announced a separate nationwide application deadline or confirmed that a fresh application window for all 600 beneficiaries is currently open. However, its general Business Incubation Programme guidelines provide for registration through the Fund’s area offices. Interested artisans can visit the nearest ITF area office to obtain and complete the business incubation application form. They can also visit the Fund’s official website, www.itf.gov.ng, for information about its programmes and application procedures. Tailors who did not participate in SUPA must ensure they obtain the required ITF certification and licence to meet the eligibility conditions. The ITF’s general business incubation guidelines also state that participation in the incubation programme is free. Applicants should note that registering for SUPA or submitting an application for the general business incubation programme does not automatically guarantee selection for the Renewed Hope Tailors initiative. Although 150 beneficiaries have already been selected from the North-Central zone, the ITF has yet to provide a detailed selection timetable for the remaining 450 places. The Director-General of ITF, Dr Afiz Oluwatoyin Ogun, represented by the Director of Legal Services, Safiya Abubakar, said the initiative aligned with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope agenda, which seeks to upgrade the skills of Nigerian artisans to international standards. According to her, the programme would provide selected tailors with a structured opportunity to develop their businesses from start-up level to maturity over five years. She urged prospective beneficiaries to pay attention to the programme’s processes and requirements. items.title: SBP issues Rs200 commemorative coin to mark Mata Sahib Hasi Devi’s 200th birth anniversary
items.description: The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) has issued a Rs200 commemorative coin to mark the 200th birth anniversary of Pujya Mata Sahib Hasi Devi, the bank said in a statement on Friday. Mata Sahib Hasi Devi was the fifth head of the historic Shadani Darbar located in the Hayat Pitafi area of Sukkur division’s Ghotki district. According to the statement, the coin has been issued through the exchange counters of all field offices of the SBP Banking Services Corporation from Friday. The coin is made of cupro-nickel, comprising 75 per cent copper and 25pc nickel. It measures 30 millimetres in diameter and weighs 13.5 grammes, the statement said. It added that the face of the coin features a waxing crescent moon and five-pointed star in the centre, facing northwest in a rising position. Along the periphery on top of the crescent and star is inscribed “ Islami Jamhuria Pakistan ” (Islamic Republic of Pakistan) in Urdu. Below the crescent, at the top of the two wheat springs with their arms curved upwards, is the year of issuance 2026. The coin’s value and “ rupia ” in Urdu script are inscribed on the right and left sides of the crescent and star, respectively. Meanwhile, the back features a picture of Puj Shandani Darbar in the centre. The inscription “Pujya Mata Sahib Hasi Devi” appears at the top along the periphery, while the wording “200th birth anniversary” is written along the lower periphery. The years 1826 and 2026 are written on the left and right sides of the picture, respectively, marking the 200th birth anniversary, the statement said. Last month, Pakistan Post also issued two special commemorative postage stamps and a souvenir sheet for the 200th birth anniversary of Mata Sahib Hasi Devi to promote interfaith harmony and Sufi traditions in the region.

items.title: Faux, cette déclaration n’est pas du président de la Transition
items.description: Une video largement relayee sur TikTok attribue au president de la Transition, le general d'armee Assimi Goïta, des propos demandant a son homologue ivoirien, Alassane Ouattara, de recuperer les ressortissants ivoiriens presents au Mali. Si les images sont authentiques, la bande sonore, elle, a ete modifiee. Sur TikTok, la sequence montre Assimi Goïta en tenue militaire, devant un micro. Une voix accompagnee de sous-titres lui prete cette declaration : « Alassane, arrange-toi pour venir chercher les Ivoiriens qui sont ici ». Dans les commentaires, plusieurs internautes semblent prendre ces propos pour une veritable declaration du chef de l'etat malien. Pourtant, la video est trompeuse. Des images authentiques, mais une voix modifiee Une recherche d'image inversee a permis de retrouver la sequence originale, datee du 22 septembre 2026. La comparaison des deux videos montre que les propos attribues a Assimi Goïta ne correspondent pas a son intervention initiale. La bande sonore presente egalement une difference de voix. Cette manipulation est aussi relevee par l'Agence ivoirienne de presse. Selon sa verification, les images diffusees sont authentiques, mais la bande sonore a ete modifiee. Autrement dit, une veritable sequence du president malien a ete utilisee pour lui faire tenir des propos qu'il n'a pas prononces dans l'intervention originale. D'autres videos similaires sur le meme compte Un autre element merite l'attention. Le compte a l'origine de la publication diffuse egalement des videos similaires attribuant de fausses declarations au president de la Transition burkinabe, le capitaine Ibrahim Traore. Certaines de ces sequences cumulent des centaines de milliers de vues. Ces publications montrent comment des images reelles peuvent etre detournees par une modification de leur bande sonore pour faire croire a de fausses declarations. Avant de croire ou de partager une video, il est donc important de verifier sa source, de rechercher sa version originale et de comparer les elements sonores. L'historique du compte qui la publie peut egalement fournir des indices utiles. Lire aussi : une video manipulee attribue de faux propos a Assimi Goïta sur les orpailleurs expulses de Guinee L’article Faux, cette déclaration n’est pas du président de la Transition est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: Nigeria’s future depends on mentally resilient youths — Mamora
items.description: Former minister urges graduates to embrace purpose, adaptability, continuous learning By Adeola Badru Former Minister of Health, Olorunnimbe Mamora, has said Nigeria’s future depends largely on the mental resilience, character development and sense of purpose of its youths, warning that academic qualifications alone are insufficient to prepare them for the challenges of the modern world. Mamora said young Nigerians must develop the capacity to navigate economic uncertainties, technological disruptions and changing employment opportunities through adaptability, continuous learning and problem-solving skills. He spoke while delivering the 18th Convocation Lecture of Ajayi Crowther University (ACU), Oyo, titled, “Youths’ Mental Health and Purpose: Thriving in a Volatile World.” The former minister challenged graduating students to look beyond the certificates they had earned and prepare for a world where success would increasingly depend on their ability to manage uncertainty, identify opportunities and remain relevant. He described convocation as a transition into a new phase of life, requiring graduates to demonstrate resilience, discipline, adaptability and a clear sense of purpose. Mamora identified the growing influence of social media, economic pressures and rapid technological advancement as emerging challenges to the mental wellbeing of young people. While acknowledging that the internet had expanded access to information and opportunities, he noted that excessive engagement with digital platforms could contribute to loneliness, anxiety and unhealthy comparisons. He urged graduates not to measure their achievements or personal worth against the lifestyles and apparent successes of others on social media. “Do not allow social media platforms to become the mirror through which you measure your worth. “Your value is not determined by the number of people who like your photograph. Stop comparing your backstage with somebody else’s stage,” he said. On the changing employment landscape, particularly with the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Mamora said graduates must recognise that education should go beyond acquiring academic qualifications. He stressed the importance of critical thinking, problem-solving, skills acquisition and continuous learning, noting that adaptability would be essential to remaining relevant in the evolving world of work. Drawing inspiration from the life of Bishop Samuel Ajayi Crowther, after whom the university was named, Mamora said the cleric’s journey from slavery to becoming a renowned missionary and scholar demonstrated the importance of determination and resilience in overcoming adversity. He urged the graduates to draw inspiration from Crowther’s life and remain committed to their aspirations despite the challenges they might encounter. The former minister also challenged young Nigerians to move beyond waiting for paid employment and begin identifying problems in their communities for which they could develop practical solutions. He said youths should see themselves as contributors to national development, adding that innovation and enterprise could create opportunities for both personal advancement and collective progress. Addressing substance abuse, Mamora cautioned young people against turning to drugs as a means of escaping life’s pressures. He described substance dependence as a potential “cage or catastrophic bondage,” urging youths to adopt healthier ways of managing stress and emotional difficulties. He recommended healthy relationships, regular exercise and adequate rest, while encouraging those experiencing mental health challenges to seek professional support when necessary. Mamora said protecting mental health was essential to achieving personal goals and making meaningful contributions to society. At the convocation ceremony, 87 individuals were awarded doctorate degrees in various disciplines. The university also conferred honorary doctorate degrees on renowned Professor of African History, Toyin Falola, and finance expert, Kayode Falowo, in recognition of their contributions to society. The ceremony was attended by the Chairman of the Board of Trustees, Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN, GCON; the Chancellor, Chief Tunde Afolabi; the Chairman of the Governing Council, Dr Olutoyin Okeowo; and the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Ebunoluwa Oduwole. Other dignitaries present included principal officers of the university, distinguished guests and parents of the graduating students. items.title: Empress Gifty to perform at 2026 Guinness Ghana DJ Awards
items.description: Ghanaian gospel musician Empress Gifty is set to perform at the 2026 Guinness Ghana DJ Awards, scheduled for Friday, December 4, at the Palms Convention Centre in Accra. Her performance will be one of the highlights of this year’s awards ceremony, which will celebrate and honour disc jockeys (DJs) for their contributions to Ghana’s music and entertainment industry. The announcement comes as anticipation builds ahead of the awards night, which is expected to bring together DJs, entertainment industry stakeholders, sponsors, media personalities and music enthusiasts. Ghanaian musician Black Sherif has also praised DJs for their role in promoting music and supporting artistes, describing them as the foundation of the music Ghana exports to the world. In a message to DJs, the award-winning artiste expressed gratitude for their contribution to the music industry and offered prayers for their success and financial prosperity. “Big ups to our DJ. We love you so much. We love you guys. It’s because of you that we stand. You guys are the roots to all the music we try to export. May God bless you. May God guide you guys. May God fill your pockets. DJs, we love you,” he said. The 2026 edition of the Guinness Ghana DJ Awards, powered by Smirnoff, was officially launched at Eden Gardens Hotel in Accra, the event’s official hospitality partner. The launch unveiled the roadmap for the new awards season, leading up to the grand ceremony and the platform’s 15th anniversary celebration next year. The grand awards ceremony is expected to be broadcast live to an estimated audience of more than 17 million viewers across 48 African countries. This year’s awards season is being held under the theme “All Out”, celebrating the passion, resilience and creativity of DJs who continue to push boundaries and shape Ghana’s entertainment industry. The organisers say the 2026 edition will feature fresh initiatives, new rewards and an expanded awards scheme, with continued support from Guinness Ghana through Smirnoff.

items.title: Centrale solaire de l’île de Kassa : « Le président Mamadi Doumbouya nous sort de l’obscurité. Kassa était oubliée…» (Laye Sékou Camara, ministre)
items.description: Le ministre de l’Énergie, Laye Sékou Camara, a pris part au lancement des travaux de construction de la centrale solaire photovoltaïque de l’île de Kassa, dans la commune de Conakry. À cette occasion, il a salué les initiatives du président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, en faveur de cette localité, tout en insistant sur l’impact social attendu de cette infrastructure énergétique. Dans son intervention, le ministre a d’abord rendu grâce à Dieu avant d’exprimer sa reconnaissance au chef de l’État pour les actions engagées en faveur de Kassa. « Je voudrais commencer par remercier le Tout-Puissant Allah, qui nous a permis de nous réunir ici aujourd’hui. Je tiens également à remercier le général Mamadi Doumbouya, qui a sorti Kassa de l’obscurité. Kassa était oubliée. Le président a décidé lui-même de venir habiter à Kassa. Nous venons également d’y célébrer le Mining Summit. Aujourd’hui encore, nous lançons les travaux de construction de la centrale solaire photovoltaïque de Kassa », a-t-il déclaré. Pour Laye Sékou Camara, cette nouvelle infrastructure traduit la volonté des autorités de renforcer l’accès à l’électricité dans cette île de la capitale. Il estime que les travaux devraient être achevés dans quelques mois. Le ministre a également tenu à faire une distinction entre une simple cérémonie de pose de première pierre et le démarrage effectif d’un chantier. Il affirme avoir exigé que les travaux soient réellement engagés avant de prendre part à la cérémonie. « J’avais dit au directeur général que je ne viendrais pas pour une simple pose de première pierre s’il n’y avait pas de travaux à réaliser. Dieu merci, les travaux ont effectivement démarré. Je tiens donc à préciser qu’il s’agit du démarrage effectif des travaux et non d’une simple pose de première pierre », a-t-il insisté. Au-delà des caractéristiques techniques de l’installation, le ministre de l’Énergie a surtout mis l’accent sur les retombées sociales du projet. Selon lui, l’importance de cette centrale ne doit pas être appréciée uniquement à travers sa puissance ou la taille de ses équipements, mais à travers le nombre de ménages qui pourront bénéficier de l’électricité. « Ce qui est important, ce n’est pas la grandeur de la centrale, mais plutôt son impact social sur les populations de Kassa. Combien de ménages vont ainsi sortir de l’obscurité ? », a-t-il souligné. Abordant les perspectives d’extension de l’infrastructure, Laye Sékou Camara a indiqué que la centrale, dont la capacité actuelle est estimée à un peu plus de 600 kilowatts, pourrait connaître une augmentation significative de sa puissance. « Cette centrale est évolutive. Nous sommes actuellement à un peu plus de 600 kilowatts. Bientôt, nous allons négocier avec l’entreprise pour porter sa capacité à 2 ou 3 mégawatts », a-t-il annoncé. Le ministre a enfin invité à ne pas minimiser ce projet en raison de la taille initiale de ses installations, rappelant que sa véritable portée devra se mesurer aux changements qu’il apportera dans le quotidien des habitants de l’île de Kassa. Kassa était oubliée…» (Laye Sékou Camara, ministre) est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Road signs not for adverts or political campaigns – NRSA warns
items.description: The National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) has cautioned businesses, religious organisations and political parties against using road signs and other road infrastructure for advertising, publicity and campaign activities, warning that the practice poses serious risks to road safety. The Authority said it had observed an increasing trend of posters, banners and promotional materials being attached to road signs, traffic signs, road medians, gantries and other public infrastructure, with some existing signs being defaced or obstructed in the process. It described the development as unlawful and warned that such activities could compromise the safety of motorists, motorcyclists, cyclists and pedestrians who rely on road signs for essential traffic information. In a statement, the NRSA stressed that road signs were installed primarily to regulate traffic, provide directions and alert road users to potential hazards, rather than serve as spaces for promotional activities. “Road signs and road infrastructure are provided primarily to regulate, guide, and inform road users. They are not authorised spaces for commercial advertising, religious or political campaign displays,” the Authority stated. It explained that obstructing or altering road signs could prevent drivers from accessing critical information needed to make safe and timely decisions, increasing the likelihood of confusion and road traffic crashes. “Covering, altering, obstructing or distracting attention from these signs can impair road users’ ability to make safe and timely decisions, increase the risk of confusion and contribute to road traffic crashes,” it warned. The Authority further noted that materials placed on road medians, gantries and other unauthorised locations could obstruct visibility and distract motorists, creating additional dangers for pedestrians and other road users. It said the risks were particularly significant for people unfamiliar with particular routes, who depend on road signs and directional information to navigate safely. NRSA warns of sanctions against offenders The Authority has consequently urged businesses, religious groups, political parties, candidates, supporters and campaign organisers to immediately stop attaching posters, banners and other publicity materials to road signs and infrastructure. It advised the groups to ensure that promotional and campaign materials were displayed only at locations approved by the relevant authorities. As part of enforcement measures, the NRSA said it would collaborate with road and local government authorities to identify and remove unauthorised materials from public infrastructure. “The Authority will work with the appropriate road and local government authorities to identify and remove unauthorised posters, banners and other materials placed on road signs and road infrastructure,” it said. It further cautioned that individuals and organisations responsible for the violations could face financial liability or be referred to the appropriate authorities for action under applicable laws. “Persons and groups responsible for such violations may also be surcharged or referred to the appropriate authorities for further action under applicable laws,” the statement added. The NRSA called on the public to demonstrate greater responsibility in the use of public infrastructure, emphasising that promotional and political activities should not undermine road safety. “Acts of publicity must never compromise the safety of road users,” the Authority stressed.

items.title: Saint-Vincent-et-les-Grenadines réitère son soutien à l’intégrité territoriale du Maroc sur son Sahara
items.description: Saint-Vincent-et-les-Grenadines a réitéré, vendredi à Rabat, son soutien à l’intégrité territoriale du Maroc sur son Sahara et au Plan marocain d’autonomie en tant qu'unique solution crédible, sérieuse et réaliste. Dans un communiqué conjoint signé à l'issue de la rencontre tenue entre le ministre des Affaires étrangères, de la Coopération africaine et des Marocains résidant à l’étranger, Nasser Bourita et le ministre des Affaires étrangères, du Commerce extérieur, des Investissements étrangers et des Affaires de la diaspora de Saint-Vincent-et-les- Grenadines, Dwight Fitzgerald Bramble, Saint-Vincent-et-les-Grenadines a réitéré « son soutien à l’intégrité territoriale du Royaume du Maroc sur l'ensemble de son territoire, y compris la région du Sahara ». Dans ce communiqué, Fitzgerald Bramblele a réaffirmé « son appui au Plan marocain d’autonomie en tant qu’unique solution crédible, sérieuse et réaliste à ce différend régional ». Saint-Vincent-et-les- Grenadines s’est également félicitée du consensus international croissant et du momentum impulsé par le Roi Mohammed VI en faveur du plan d’autonomie marocain. Dans une déclaration à la presse à l’issue de cette rencontre, Fitzgerald Bramble a relevé l’engagement réaffirmé de son pays envers la souveraineté du Maroc, ainsi que le soutien de Saint-Vincent-et-les- Grenadines au Royaume dans la protection de son territoire et de sa population. En sa qualité de membre de l’Organisation des États de la Caraïbe orientale (OECO), Saint-Vincent-et-les- Grenadines s’est félicitée de l’ouverture de l’Ambassade de l’OECO à Rabat, le 18 octobre 2018, ainsi que du Consulat général de l’Organisation à Dakhla, le 31 mars 2022. Le communiqué souligne que ces représentations constituent une opportunité importante pour renforcer davantage les échanges et la coopération entre le Royaume du Maroc et les États membres de l’OECO. items.title: Early BECE registration fuels examination malpractice – Africa Education Watch
items.description: The Executive Director of Africa Education Watch, Kofi Asare, has defended the Education Minister’s directive restricting the premature registration of candidates for the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE), arguing that the practice undermines the integrity of the national assessment system. He says the practice allows some parents to manipulate the examination registration process by arranging for their children to be presented as final-year Junior High School (JHS) students before completing the required three years of basic education. Speaking on the ongoing debate surrounding the directive, Mr Asare explained that the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) requires BECE school candidates to obtain 30 per cent of their overall results from continuous assessment, with the remaining 70 per cent coming from the final examination. He said the continuous assessment component is accumulated across JHS One, Two and Three, meaning candidates are expected to complete all three years before sitting the examination. However, he alleged that some parents collude with school authorities to fabricate the missing JHS Three continuous assessment records for children who have been fast-tracked into the examination. “Immediately a child jumps JHS Three, invariably, the meaning is that a headteacher somewhere will cook a JHS Three continuous assessment for that child,” he said. According to him, the arrangement involves parents and school heads creating the impression that the child has completed the required three years before being presented to WAEC as a final-year student. Mr Asare disclosed that Africa Education Watch began investigating the practice around 2021 and uncovered instances where parents allegedly paid substantial amounts to secure early BECE registration for their children. He cited investigations conducted around the Osino area in 2023, where some parents were reportedly paying as much as GH¢10,000 to fast-track their children’s examination registration. He explained that some parents, particularly those whose children attended private JHS institutions, travelled from Accra to schools in outlying communities to secure the arrangement. The practice, he said, was partly driven by the introduction of the 30 per cent Category A placement protocol for candidates from public junior high schools. Some parents reportedly sought to have their children registered through public schools to benefit from the placement arrangement while simultaneously cutting short a year of their children’s education. Mr Asare maintained that the practice goes beyond accelerating the academic progression of gifted children, describing the fabrication of continuous assessment records as examination malpractice that threatens the credibility of the BECE. He stressed that talented children should have the opportunity to benefit from accelerated placement, but insisted that such arrangements must be based on an independent assessment of their academic abilities and socio-emotional development. “Talented kids have the right to be identified and assessed independently and based on their talents, both academic and socio-emotional, and given accelerated placement. That should happen,” he said. He added that having a structured framework for identifying gifted learners should not be confused with the alleged manipulation of examination records to facilitate premature BECE registration.

items.title: Ukraine: Meaning-Making Workshop Outcome Document: Cross-Cutting Demographic Realities for 2027 HNRP Planning
items.description: Country: Ukraine Sources: CARE, NGO Girls, Protection Cluster, Ukraine Gender in Humanitarian Action Working Group, UN Women Please refer to the attached file. Single-layer vulnerability classifications obscure the dynamic, intersectional realities of the current crisis. Moving beyond status-based or geographic targeting to needs-based response requires anchoring interventions in actual socio-economic and demographic profiles derived from the latest assessments (MSNA, COD-PS, DTM, Rapid Gender Assessment, and specialized TWG consultations). This document presents the outcomes of the Meaning-Making Workshop 2026, consolidating gender, age, and disability considerations and translating them into actionable recommendations for the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) 2027. The document was shared with and presented to the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG), which brings together sector and cluster leads, in September 2026. It brings together the key materials and findings from the workshop, organized by the Gender in Humanitarian Action Working Group (GiHA WG) in collaboration with the Cross-Cutting Expertise Group—which includes the GiHA WG, Age and Disability Technical Working Group (TWG), Accountability to Affected People Working Group (AAP WG), and LGBTIQ+ Technical Working Group—as well as the Data Coordination Group, comprising REACH, IOM, and OCHA.

items.title: Omo-Agege denies snubbing police invitation over Uduere killings
items.description: Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has denied reports claiming he refused to honour an invitation from the Delta State Police Command over Monday’s attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, at Uduere. In a statement on Friday by his Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, the former Deputy President of the Senate said he had seen the reports and described them as untrue. “Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has seen the reports claiming he refused to honour an invitation from the Delta State Police Command over Monday’s attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, at Uduere. “It isn’t true. You can’t turn down an invitation you never received,” he said. According to the statement, no formal invitation has reached the Senator or his office. “No letter has reached the Senator or his office, and no officer has come to him with one. He first learned of it the same way everyone else did, from the Command’s announcement in the media.” Areh said the report that Omo-Agege refused to appear was based on a single unnamed source. “The claim that he refused leans on a single unnamed source. The Senator hasn’t told the police, or anyone else, that he won’t appear.” The statement also revisited the events at Uduere, insisting that Omo-Agege was the victim of the attack. “It is worth remembering what happened at Uduere. Senator Omo-Agege was the target of an assassination attempt. Senior members of his campaign team were murdered, and others are still in hospital with serious injuries. “He is the one who survived an attack on his life, and the one demanding that those responsible be found and prosecuted.” Omo-Agege said he wants the case resolved and justice for the victims. “He wants this case resolved, and he wants justice for the dead and the wounded. If the police serve a lawful invitation, he will honour it. He asks only that it be sent through his office so a date can be agreed.” He faulted the manner in which the alleged invitation was made public. “A summons announced in the press before it reaches the person named is not due process, and he won’t be tried in the media,” he said. items.title: 2027: National Counter Terrorism Centre moves to foil attacks on INEC facilities, personnel
items.description: ..Laka warns against electoral violence, voter intimidation, destruction of infrastructure By Kingsley Omonobi The National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC), Office of the National Security Adviser, has said it is working with security agencies to prevent planned attacks on Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) offices, personnel and electoral infrastructure ahead of the 2027 general elections. The National Coordinator of the Centre, Major General Adamu Laka, also said measures were being strengthened to protect voters and prevent emerging security threats from disrupting the electoral process. Laka spoke at the National Flag-off/North Central Zone Town Hall Engagement on Preventing Electoral Violence and Strengthening Election Security in Nigeria. He urged youths not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of political violence, describing them as critical stakeholders in the country’s democratic future. “In this regard, I urge our young people not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of political violence. You are important stakeholders in Nigeria’s democratic future and your energy, creativity and influence should be directed towards promoting peace, tolerance and responsible civic participation,” he said. He said the Centre was working towards preventing attacks on INEC offices and personnel, protecting voters and electoral infrastructure, countering fake news and inflammatory narratives, strengthening community-based early warning systems and ensuring timely responses to emerging security threats. Describing elections as the heartbeat of democracy, Laka said their credibility depended not only on the conduct of voting and announcement of results but also on the peace, security and public confidence surrounding the entire electoral process. “There is absolutely no gain in any loss of life or property as a result of this democratic process,” he said. The NCTC coordinator identified misinformation and disinformation, hate speech, political intolerance, incitement, youth manipulation, political thuggery, vote buying, voter intimidation, voter suppression and destruction of public infrastructure as factors that could fuel electoral violence. He said stakeholders must collectively address the threats and strengthen early warning and response mechanisms to identify potential dangers before they escalate into violence. Laka also stressed the need to build public confidence in the electoral process and ensure that women, youths, persons with disabilities and internally displaced persons were not excluded from meaningful participation. He maintained that preventing electoral violence was not the responsibility of security agencies alone but required the collective commitment of political actors, government institutions, traditional and religious leaders, civil society organisations, the media and community-based organisations. The National Coordinator commended the Centre for Civil-Military Cooperation (CIMICO) for partnering with the NCTC to organise the nationwide campaign. He said the NCTC would provide coordination and technical leadership, while CIMICO and other partners would support community-level engagement, awareness creation and trust-building initiatives. He added that collaboration with INEC, the Nigeria Police Force, the National Orientation Agency, other security agencies and development partners would help extend the campaign to communities across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. “Our objective is clear: to ensure that the 2027 general elections are peaceful, credible, inclusive and secure, free from electoral violence and intimidation,” he said. Laka called on political parties and their supporters to embrace issue-based campaigns, respect the rule of law and demonstrate political maturity, warning that the pursuit of political power should not undermine the lives, security and unity of Nigerians. He said the success of the campaign would be measured not by the number of meetings held or speeches delivered but by its impact on communities, public awareness, the effectiveness of early warning and response mechanisms, and the ability of citizens to participate in elections without fear. He urged stakeholders to translate the commitments made at the town hall into practical actions across their communities. Earlier, Dr Adams Otakwu of the Centre for Civil-Military Cooperation said the nationwide programme was designed to ensure that discussions on electoral violence prevention translated into practical actions, institutional commitments and measurable results. He said the engagements would be guided by five core pillars, including building a deeper understanding of the risks and consequences of electoral violence, clarifying the responsibilities of institutions and stakeholders, adopting a common methodology for the town hall meetings, ensuring follow-up on recommendations, and promoting continuity and sustainability. According to him, the programme would involve open discussions, identification of local risk factors, consideration of early warning mechanisms, experience sharing and the development of practical recommendations. Otakwu said the organisers would also monitor the implementation of resolutions to ensure that the outcomes of the engagements reached communities at the grassroots and across the country. He stressed that election security should not be treated as the exclusive responsibility of security agencies, noting that citizens and other stakeholders also had important roles to play in preventing violence. He added that electoral violence prevention was a continuous process that extended beyond election day. “There has to be timely information exchange. There has to be community vigilance so that at every point that anything is sensed to be a trigger of electoral violence, we’ll be able to promptly report it to legitimate security institutions,” he said. The post 2027: National Counter Terrorism Centre moves to foil attacks on INEC facilities, personnel appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: OK Movement withdraws support for Obi, Kwankwaso, NDC
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- THE OK Movement, a political support platform associated with the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential ticket of Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso, has withdrawn its support for the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC. According to the group, its national leadership has formally been made to understand that the presidential candidate of the NDC,Obi, and the party he represents have decided to discontinue their political relationship with the OK Movement. In a statement on Friday by the National Director General of OK Movement, Hon. John Ozyl Ughulu, he said Politics is a game of numbers, and numbers play a decisive role in determining electoral strength, political relevance and, ultimately, the outcome of elections. Ughulu who disclised that the OK Movement will, in due course, announce its preferred political party and presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections, said they have already commenced engagements with other political parties and potential presidential candidates whose political vision, leadership capacity and ideological commitments align with our established principles and values. The National Director-General of OK Movement who noted that the organisation remained focused on the task ahead and firmly believe that their organisational strength cuts across wards, local governments and states of the federation, adding, “Our grassroots presence, organisational reach and mobilisation capacity position the OK Movement as a formidable independent political force capable of influencing the outcome of the 2027 general elections and challenging the present administration. “Our data are clear. Our structures speak for us. Our ideology defines us. The OK Movement remains independent in its identity, organisational structure and political decisions. No individual, political party or political interest owns this movement. “The National Leadership of the OK Movement has formally been made to understand that the presidential candidate of the NDC, His Excellency Peter Obi, and the party he represents have decided to discontinue their political relationship with the OK Movement. “While we consider this development regrettable, we respect the decision and sincerely appreciate His Excellency for the time, engagements and opportunities shared with our movement. “Following this development, the National Leadership of the OK Movement has resolved to officially discontinue all campaign, mobilisation and operational support for the NDC Party, effective immediately. “Consequently, all OK Movement political structures and operational engagements at the ward, local government and state levels are hereby withdrawn from the NDC’s campaign and mobilisation activities. “We recognise that the NDC has a considerable social media following which, if properly organised and translated into meaningful grassroots political participation, could deliver significant electoral benefits. The responsibility for converting that support into electoral strength now rests with the party and its leadership.” Ughulu further said, “The OK Movement believes that leadership must be defined by capacity, competence, integrity and the ability to resolve issues. “A true leader must possess the wisdom, courage and emotional intelligence to manage disagreements, build bridges and unite people rather than encourage division or benefit from internal conflicts. “Leadership must never be about personal interests, self-centred ambitions or the pursuit of supremacy. It must be about selflessness, honesty, accountability and the willingness to place collective interests above personal considerations. “Nigeria desperately needs this quality of leadership at this critical moment in our national history.” On their next political direction, the National Director General, said, “The OK Movement will, in due course, announce its preferred political party and presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections. “We have already commenced engagements with other political parties and potential presidential candidates whose political vision, leadership capacity and ideological commitments align with our established principles and values. “We remain focused on the task ahead and firmly believe that our organisational strength cuts across wards, local governments and states of the federation. “Our grassroots presence, organisational reach and mobilisation capacity position the OK Movement as a formidable independent political force capable of influencing the outcome of the 2027 general elections and challenging the present administration. “Our data are clear. Our structures speak for us. Our ideology defines us. “The OK Movement remains independent in its identity, organisational structure and political decisions. No individual, political party or political interest owns this movement.” Ughulu who noted that their fundamental principles remain no – negotiable, said, ” we remain committed to the fundamental principles of: Integrity, Fairness, Equity, Justice, Competence, Accountability and National Unity. “These principles are not negotiable, nor will we compromise them for political convenience. “We will not allow intimidation, manipulation, personal interests or anyone’s selfish political ambition to determine the political direction of our movement. “The OK Movement is bigger than any individual. It was established on principles, built through collective sacrifice and remains committed to the Nigerian people and the ideals upon which it was founded. “The National Leadership wishes to express its profound appreciation to every member, coordinator, volunteer and supporter of the OK Movement for their resilience, sacrifices and unwavering commitment. “We understand that some members may have developed strong political and emotional attachments to the NDC Party and may feel disappointed by this development and the decision we have taken. “We respect the personal convictions and political choices of every member. Anyone who chooses to maintain their relationship with the NDC or pursue a different political direction is entitled to do so without intimidation, hostility or resentment. “However, we must distinguish between individual political choices and the collective institutional decisions of the OK Movement. “We recognise the time, resources, energy and personal sacrifices invested in building this movement across the country. We assure every member that these sacrifices have not been in vain. They remain an important part of our collective journey towards building a better Nigeria. “We therefore urge all coordinators and members to remain calm, disciplined and focused while awaiting further directives from the National Leadership.” The post OK Movement withdraws support for Obi, Kwankwaso, NDC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ADC waste plan will create 21,000 jobs in Lagos – Gbadamosi
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African Democratic Congress (ADC) deputy governorship candidate Babatunde Olalere Gbadamosi has projected that the party’s waste management plan would create at least 21,000 jobs in Lagos, including 20,000 for waste collection crews. Gbadamosi, who is running with ADC governorship candidate Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, spoke at the Road to Election 2027 Lagos Deputy Governorship Debate on Nigeria Info FM on Friday, where he outlined proposals on employment, waste collection, housing and transportation. Addressing unemployment, Gbadamosi said he did not know the state’s unemployment rate and disputed figures published by the Lagos government. He proposed a review of public sector salaries and said his plans for waste management, housing, transportation and education would create jobs for Lagosians. “First of all, the truth is, I suppose the truth is, I really don’t know what the unemployment rate is. Whatever figures that are put out by the APC government of Lagos State are usually just false. They just manufacture figures, yank them out of their a**,” he said. He said he and Rhodes-Vivour had agreed to “undertake a review, a wholesale review of public sector salaries, in order to bring them in line with our current economic realities.” He also cited plans for 20,000 jobs in waste-to-energy, 100,000 affordable housing units and 16,000 electric buses. “We plan to bring 16,000 electric buses into Lagos State because we simply don’t have enough capacity to carry the 24 million people of Lagos State on the current transportation system,” he said, adding that the housing and transport plans would also provide work for young people. On waste collection, Gbadamosi proposed providing each local government with at least 200 dumpsters. He estimated that 4,000 trucks, each with a five-person crew, would create 20,000 jobs. “All right, we have 20 local governments. So 200 times 20, that’s 4000 trucks. 4000 trucks times five crew members, each. That’s already 20,000 jobs,” he said. He estimated that recycling centres would create at least another 1,000 jobs, based on a minimum of 50 workers at each of 20 local government centres. “That’s 50 jobs times 20 local governments. That’s already what 1000 extra jobs minimum,” he said, adding that the programme would be funded with “25% of Lagos State revenue that is being paid to Alpha Beta at the moment.” Other major contenders at the debate included Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) deputy governorship candidate Moriam Tolani Animashaun and Social Democratic Party (SDP) deputy candidate Kayode Evelyn Aderiyike. The debate was hosted by Kofi Bartels and Ireti Bakare-Yusuf. The post ADC waste plan will create 21,000 jobs in Lagos – Gbadamosi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: PANDEF rejects 20% NCDMB fund deduction for research council
items.description: …Warns against diversion of local content funds, urges NASS to review proposed legislation By Henry Umoru ABUJA – The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF), the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, has rejected the proposed 20 per cent deduction from the Nigerian Content Development Fund to finance the proposed National Council on Research, Science, Technology and Innovation. The forum warned that the move could undermine years of investment in indigenous industrial capacity and weaken the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB), which has been instrumental in promoting local expertise, skills acquisition, enterprise development and industrialisation. PANDEF urged the National Assembly to review Section 19 of the proposed legislation establishing the council and reject the provision earmarking 20 per cent of the Nigerian Content Development Fund for its financing. Addressing journalists in Abuja on Friday, PANDEF National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, acknowledged the Federal Government’s efforts to strengthen the country’s research, science, technology and innovation capacity but expressed concern over Part IV, Section 19(a) of the proposed Bill. He described the proposed funding arrangement as inappropriate, counterproductive and fundamentally flawed, arguing that a new national institution should not be financed by weakening an existing statutory agency with clearly defined responsibilities and ongoing development commitments. Igali said the NCDMB, which commenced operations in 2010, had a statutory mandate to promote the development, acquisition and application of indigenous capacity in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry. He noted that the Nigerian Content Development Fund was already supporting strategic investments in the oil and gas sector and related areas, including agriculture, manufacturing and transportation. According to him, diverting 20 per cent of the fund could disrupt existing commitments, constrain ongoing investments and slow the progress recorded in local content development. “The Nigerian Content Development Fund is not an idle pool of resources awaiting allocation. It is an active development instrument that is already financing and supporting several strategic investments in the oil and gas industry and related sectors of the Nigerian economy,” he said. Igali also warned that the proposed funding mechanism could establish a dangerous precedent in public finance, whereby newly established government institutions would depend on deductions from funds already allocated to existing statutory agencies. He said such an arrangement was inconsistent with sound corporate governance and fiscal policy, stressing that new institutions should have independent, predictable and sustainable funding structures. “The principle of sound public finance requires that the establishment of new institutions should be accompanied by deliberate, independent and sustainable funding arrangements. “It is inappropriate to weaken one institution in order to finance another, particularly when the existing institution is performing effectively and fulfilling its statutory mandate,” he said. The PANDEF chairman further stressed that the Niger Delta had a legitimate interest in protecting the financial strength of the NCDMB, given its contributions to human capital development and economic empowerment across the region. He said the board’s interventions had supported education, technical and vocational training, skills acquisition, enterprise development and the growth of indigenous businesses in Niger Delta communities. According to him, reducing the fund’s resources would limit the board’s capacity to expand these programmes in a region that had historically borne the environmental and socio-economic consequences of oil and gas exploration. Igali called on the National Assembly to critically review the funding provisions in Section 19 of the proposed Bill and identify alternative sources of financing for the proposed council. “We call on the National Assembly to critically review the funding provisions contained in Section 19 of the proposed Bill and reject the proposed 20 per cent deduction from the Nigerian Content Development Fund. “We believe that the proposed council deserves a dedicated, predictable and sustainable funding framework that will enable it to discharge its responsibilities without undermining the mandates and financial capacities of existing statutory institutions,” he said. He added that the funding provision could be referred to the Executive for further review, if necessary, to develop a more appropriate and sustainable arrangement. Igali disclosed that PANDEF had already communicated its position to the President of the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives, urging them to give the matter serious consideration. The forum, however, reaffirmed its support for the Federal Government’s efforts to advance research, science and technology, insisting that the pursuit of new national initiatives should not come at the expense of existing institutions. “We must not sacrifice the gains of local content development in the pursuit of a new national initiative. “We urge the Federal Government and the National Assembly to protect and strengthen the NCDMB and its Fund, recognising their strategic contributions to indigenous capacity development, industrialisation, employment generation and economic diversification,” he said. Also speaking, a member of PANDEF and former Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Labour and Productivity, Dr Timiebi Koripamo-Agary, questioned the need to establish another institution to oversee research, science, technology and innovation, arguing that existing agencies should instead be strengthened. She cited the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI) and the Projects Development Institute (PRODA) as institutions with existing capacities that could be enhanced to deliver on the proposed council’s objectives. Recalling the contributions of indigenous technology institutions during the Nigerian Civil War, Koripamo-Agary noted that some of the agencies established to develop local technological capacity still existed but faced funding challenges. “Why not think out of the box about how to strengthen the capacity of NASENI? There are other agencies that can do what is being proposed,” she said. She also questioned the proposed funding source, suggesting that the government explore alternative revenue options, including taxation of telecommunications companies, rather than drawing resources from the Nigerian Content Development Fund. “If it’s about communication, how about taxing them and deploying part of the money that they are making? And they are making so much money,” she said. Koripamo-Agary further expressed concern over poor budget implementation and the rollover of allocations across financial years. She urged the government to improve coordination among institutions, strengthen existing agencies and deploy available resources more effectively, arguing that Nigeria could pursue new initiatives without weakening institutions already performing related functions. The post PANDEF rejects 20% NCDMB fund deduction for research council appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Burkina Faso : L’ONEA confie la confection des tenues de travail de ses agents à TEXFORCES-BF
items.description: Dans le but de développer et de renforcer un partenariat stratégique dans des domaines d'intérêts communs, l'Office national de l'eau et de l'assainissement (ONEA) et le complexe industriel TEXFORCES-BF ont signé, ce 25 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou, une convention portant sur la conception et la fabrication des tenues de travail du personnel de l'ONEA. Cet accord illustre la volonté de privilégier la production nationale et de valoriser le coton burkinabè ainsi que le savoir-faire industriel local. Lors de la cérémonie de signature, Flandion Idrissa SOURABIE , Directeur Général de l'ONEA, a souligné que la souveraineté économique se bâtit à travers les décisions concrètes des entreprises publiques. En choisissant TEXFORCES-BF pour concevoir les équipements de ses équipes, l'office fait le pari de mobiliser les compétences nationales afin de répondre aux besoins essentiels de son service public. L'accord prévoit la confection des tenues destinées à l'ensemble du personnel de l'ONEA. « Quand un agent de l'ONEA revêtira une tenue confectionnée ici à partir du coton burkinabè, il portera le fruit du travail de nos producteurs et du savoir-faire de nos équipes industrielles » , a-t-il indiqué. De son côté, TEXFORCES-BF s'engage à honorer ses obligations avec rigueur, professionnalisme et responsabilité, en veillant à la qualité des équipements, au respect des spécifications techniques et aux délais de livraison. Karzoum Eugène SONDO, Directeur Général de TEXFORCES-BF a saisi cette occasion pour lancer un appel aux sociétés d'État, aux collectivités et aux entreprises privées afin qu'elles s'orientent vers des tenues durables, au juste prix, fabriquées au Burkina Faso. Selon lui, cette démarche vise à mettre fin à une pratique qui voyait une grande part des tenues de travail commandées à l'extérieur, faisant ainsi sortir du pays des ressources financières issues du peuple burkinabè. « Je prends l'engagement que TEXFORCES honorera ses obligations avec rigueur, professionnalisme et responsabilité. Nous veillerons à la qualité des tenues, au respect des spécifications techniques et des délais de livraison. Nous pouvons habiller vos équipes avec des tenues durables, au juste prix, fabriquées au Burkina Faso » , a-t-il déclaré. Ce partenariat s'inscrit dans une dynamique de rupture avec l'économie de dépendance marquée par l'exportation de matières premières et l'importation de produits finis. Il accompagne la transformation portée par la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP) sous le leadership du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORE. Lazard KOLA Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : L'ONEA confie la confection des tenues de travail de ses agents à TEXFORCES-BF est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Somalia: Radio Ergo Weekly Feedback Report, Issued: 27 Nov 2026
items.description: Country: Somalia Source: Radio Ergo Please refer to the attached file. Brief Summary Commentary on rainfall and its positive impact on lives and livelihoods continued to form the bulk of the calls to Radio Ergo’s nationwide feedback platform in the week 19-25 November 2026. These calls came mostly from Jubbaland, South West, Hirshabelle, and some from Galmudug. However, some callers mainly in southern locations noted a tailing off of the rainfall, patchy areas without rain, and also intensely hot temperatures. A few in Gedo and Bay regions said they were now running short of water again. Drought conditions were cited in Bari. Several callers complained about influxes of mosquitoes and rising malaria cases, and wanted mosquito control measures. In Gedo region a number of IDP callers complained of hardships and their need for aid. The following summarises the calls by theme. Health – callers in Awdhegle in Lower Shabelle and Adado in Galgadud spoke of influxes of mosquitoes in their areas and a rise in malaria and wanted the menace to be brought under control. A caller in Gedo said the mosquitoes were causing illness with headaches and fever. A caller in Bardera said they had good rainfall, but mosquitoes were their main concern. A caller in Dollow also cited a mosquito influx, adding that despite the rain people were impoverished and aid agencies hadn’t visited the area for six months. IDPs – a caller in Iftin camp, Bardera, said they and their farms were doing well after the rain. On the other hand, a female caller in Bardera identifying as an IDP said they had received little rainfall, their crops had been attacked by pests and disease, and the schools had been shut for the past six months depriving the children of education. In Qurdubey, a caller called twice on behalf of displaced families who had lost their livestock. He said those families with a few livestock left were able to sell them for a living, but others like them were facing hardship and challenging conditions including poor sanitation. He added an appeal for aid. Aid – a caller in Dollow complained that they had been registered by aid groups a few days ago, but had not received the cash aid they thought they were going to get. Another caller, location unspecified, wanted a resumption of the cash aid they used to get from WFP that had stopped. Food Security – a caller in Bardera said he wanted to share information about the high inflation and rising costs of basics they were facing. Locusts – a caller in Kismayo said he had a farm near the airport and was concerned about locusts. He wanted to know how the farmers could protect their crops. Climate – a caller in Baidoa, Bay region, said they’d been experiencing intense heat and wanted to know if this was because of climate change. Similarly, a caller in Bahdo, Galgadud, said recent days had been intensely hot and people wondered if it was a sign of rain to come, or of climate change. Other callers in Guriel, Dollow, and Kismayo also described intense heat in their areas. Agriculture – farmers in southern and some central areas complained of pests damaging a range of produce including potatoes, beans, sesame, sorghum, maize, lettuce and tomatoes. They wanted to talk with experts on Radio Ergo’s weekly farming programme. Livestock – a caller in Bardera said his camels had dukan (trypanosomiasis) and the medicine he was injecting them with was not working. He wanted veterinary advice. Several herders in Jubbaland complained of foot and mouth affecting their herds. A caller in Beletweyne wanted to know more about how pre-export livestock inspections and certifications were processed in Somalia. Drought & water shortage – a caller in Rako-raho, Bari region, said they faced drought in the area and that many people had already migrated away. He added that they were in a desperate situation and needed the Puntland authority to reach them with aid. One caller in Dusamareb said they faced drought and conflict. Several in Bay region said the rain had been poor or had stopped already, with one describing the drying up of crops and grazing. A caller in Bardera said rainfall had been little and their farms were failing due to water shortages. A female caller said that odder and water shortage were affecting their livestock. Another female caller in Lower Juba said they weren’t having rainfall, the heat was intense, and their livestock were struggling. Rainfall – a female caller in Farjeni, Bari, said they had received some light rain. A caller in Harardhere, Mudug, said they were getting heavy rain and doing well. In Galgadud, callers spoke of decent rain in Bahdo, Guriel, Abudwak, and Adado, with several noting intense heat. In Hiran, callers in Buleburte, Af-ad, and El-gal noted good rain and conditions for their livestock and farms. Callers in Baidoa, Burhakaba, and Dinsor in Bay region cited beneficial rain. One in Bakool said the rain was short-lived and they hoped for more. In Gedo, several in different districts said they had had good rain but that in some places it had stopped. A caller in Tulo-banan said the rain was good, although they were poor and there were no jobs. A number of callers in Kismayo cited beneficial rainfall helping crops and livestock, while some noted dry areas nearby.

items.title: World AIDS Day: People still don’t have access to key HIV prevention medicine
items.description: Country: World Source: Médecins Sans Frontières Despite generic lenacapavir slowly becoming available for some, Gilead continues to stand in the way of equitable and affordable access amid urgent global need and demand. NEW YORK/JOHANNESBURG, NOVEMBER 26 — In advance of World AIDS Day on December 1, Doctors Without Borders/Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is once again calling for more people globally to have access to the highly effective HIV prevention medicine lenacapavir . This twice-yearly injectable version of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is the biggest breakthrough in HIV prevention yet, but US-based Gilead Sciences continues to block affordable access for countries around the world. This includes countries with growing HIV epidemics and ongoing humanitarian crises. As a result of its long-acting nature, lenacapavir may be especially valuable for stigmatized or criminalized populations, who often are excluded from or concerned about accessing health care. It is also a critical tool for people on the move who may struggle to access health clinics, people living in remote areas with few health care options, and people caught in humanitarian emergencies — including those in many of the communities in which MSF operates. “Gilead’s greed alone is the reason people across the globe don’t have access to lenacapavir already,” said Carlota Baptista da Silva, MSF’s global HIV/HCV access and advocacy lead. “Our teams are ready to provide it but have been left empty-handed or with very few doses to offer. We have patients in Eswatini and Zimbabwe ​ who’ve asked for this medicine and have been told it’s not an option because those countries' stocks had already been depleted. Kenya was supposed to see a priority roll-out but instead has faced severe shortages and delays in access. And communities where the lenacapavir clinical trials were held in Brazil, Argentina, Peru, and Mexico haven’t been guaranteed affordable access to it by Gilead.” A generic version of this twice-yearly PrEP made by Indian manufacturer Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA) in November. Dr. Reddy’s has agreed to sell its version of lenacapavir for $40 per person per year compared to the more than $28,000 per person per year that Gilead sells it for in the US. The first delivery of generics arrived in Zambia on the 25th November . However, generics won’t be available everywhere; dozens of middle-income countries will not have access to them because of the restrictive terms of Gilead’s licensing agreements . Countries blocked from accessing generics include most of Latin America, where HIV infections rose 25 percent between 2010 and 2025. An agreement Gilead has struck with the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) to supply lenacapavir in Latin America does little to ease concerns about access; the agreement ensures Gilead’s total control over supply in the region without revealing the price it will charge. Without the availability of generic lenacapavir, people in these countries are likely to pay far more than the $40 available elsewhere. “Even with the approval and arrival of generic lenacapavir, Gilead is still dictating which countries can access it and which cannot,” Baptista da Silva said. “The company continues to keep affordable versions of this medicine out of reach for millions by restricting which manufacturers can produce it and where they can sell it. The company could choose to expand the list of countries eligible for affordable generic versions of lenacapavir but is choosing to protect its profits instead. The only way to possibly end AIDS is to increase access to prevention tools like this one." These access gaps come amid recent funding cuts to HIV programs by many key governments, many of which have historically funded global HIV/AIDS efforts. Prevention efforts and services, particularly those targeting stigmatized populations, have been hit the hardest. “Many of our patients are caught in conflict, have been forced from their homes, or live in places with few health care options,” Baptista da Silva said. “Only having to get this medicine twice per year would make it much easier for someone to remain protected against HIV even if they’re on the move or unable to access a medical facility between injections. But they can only do that if it’s available more widely and affordable for them. It’s simply unacceptable that a single pharmaceutical company can dictate who can access this medicine and who can’t.” Lenacapavir must be available for $40 or less in all low- and middle-income countries. Governments must step in to help increase access if Gilead continues to block generics from being sold in more countries. ENDS.

items.title: Indian police say they rescued 164 foreigners trafficked for cyber fraud
items.description: Indian police said they had rescued 164 foreign nationals allegedly trafficked into the country and forced to commit online fraud, in a rare case involving victims from overseas. Fraud compounds, where international scammers lure internet users into fake romantic relationships, cryptocurrency investments and betting platforms, are common in Southeast Asia. While similar crimes are also widespread in India, it is much less common for the ringleaders to traffic foreigners into the country to perpetrate them. A police crackdown on an international cybercrime network in a suburb of the capital New Delhi resulted in the rescue of 92 Indonesian nationals and 72 Malaysians, the force said. The individuals were trafficked into India “on various pretexts, including promises of employment and lucrative opportunities”, it said in a statement late on Thursday. “After their arrival, the foreign nationals were allegedly confined and compelled to participate in cyber fraud activities.” Investigators have arrested a Malaysian national, whose role is “being investigated”, and identified two Indian handlers, police said. A United Nations report estimated this year that at least 300,000 people have been trafficked into scam compounds across Southeast Asia. New Delhi repatriated more than 2,400 Indians from cyberscam centres in neighbouring Myanmar in the past year, according to the foreign ministry.

items.title: Ouagadougou : Les ministres de la Santé de l’AES assistent au « faux départ » et reçoivent les bénédictions du Moogho Naaba
items.description: Dans le cadre de la réunion de validation de trois stratégies communes pour renforcer la coopération sanitaire, les ministres de la Santé des pays de l’Alliance des États du Sahel (AES) ont rendu visite à Sa Majesté le Moogho Naaba Baongo, ce 27 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou. À cette occasion, ils ont assisté à la traditionnelle cérémonie du « faux départ » du Moogho Naaba. Cette tradition se tient chaque vendredi au sein du palais du roi. Les ministres de la Santé du Mali, du Niger et du Burkina Faso ont découvert chaque étape de cette cérémonie ancestrale. À l’arrière-cour du palais, tous les ministres et les notables du roi sont réunis. Un premier coup de canon annonce la sortie du Moogho Naaba Baongo. Il est vêtu de rouge, signe de son départ imminent pour la guerre. Selon les récits, il serait prêt à aller en guerre pour récupérer son fétiche qui a été volé et emporté chez les Yadcé. Tour à tour, les ministres et les notables plaident auprès du roi pour qu’il renonce à son idée. Quelques instants plus tard, il rentre dans son palais et ressort vêtu de blanc pour montrer qu’il a adhéré à la requête de ses sujets. Il privilégie ainsi l’intérêt du peuple au détriment du sien. « On en ressort réconforté et ravi d’avoir vu le roi, Sa Majesté le Moogho Naaba et toute sa cour », s’est réjouie le médecin colonel-major Assa Badiallo Touré, ministre de la Santé et du Développement social du Mali. À l’issue de la cérémonie, Sa Majesté le Moogho Naaba a reçu les trois ministres de la Santé en audience. Le ministre de la Santé burkinabè, Dr Jean-Claude Kargougou, lui a rappelé le contexte de la réunion qui a abouti à la signature de trois documents stratégiques pour renforcer la coopération et bâtir une souveraineté sanitaire au sein de l’espace confédéral. À travers le Larlé Naaba, le Moogho Naaba a exprimé sa satisfaction face aux actions conjointes des pays de l’AES pour améliorer la santé des populations. Il leur a souhaité plein succès en les assurant de sa bénédiction. Cheick Habib Désiré BAYILI Faso7 L’article Ouagadougou : Les ministres de la Santé de l’AES assistent au « faux départ » et reçoivent les bénédictions du Moogho Naaba est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Roads blocked, traffic congested in Karachi for 2nd consecutive day
items.description: Karachi saw blocked roads and congested traffic for a second consecutive day on Friday as road closure alerts caused traffic to be diverted due to a protest around the Karachi Press Club (KPC). The city’s traffic police earlier announced diversions around KPC ahead of an expected protest, advising commuters to use alternative routes to avoid inconvenience. According to a press release, the traffic heading from MR Kiyani Chowk towards Saddar and Zainab Market would be diverted left from Coast Guards Mess towards the Sindh High Court (SHC) and Passport Office. It added that Sharea Faisal could be closed temporarily at Avari traffic signal. Traffic travelling from Sharea Faisal towards the airport would be diverted right from Avari traffic signal onto Fatima Jinnah Road, towards Cantt, School Road, CSD and Kala Pul, the release said. According to updates issued by the traffic police, the road from Coast Guard towards Zainab Market and Sarwar Shaheed Road was closed to traffic at around 3:20pm in view of security. Traffic from Coast Guard was being sent towards the Chowrangi Passport Office, while traffic coming from there was being directed towards Paradise Chowk, the traffic police said. The road was later re-opened to traffic as of an alert at 6:05pm. Drigh Road towards Karsaz and Sharea Faisal was closed to traffic at around 4pm, with traffic being rerouted from Drigh Road via the Rashid Minhas Flyover towards Millennium. The road was opened about half-an-hour later, but an alert was issued for heavy traffic pressure as the traffic was only running in one lane, slowing the movement of vehicles. At 5:22pm, the traffic police issued an update that the flow of traffic had been restored, with all lanes opened for traffic. It noted that peak hours were still ongoing but that traffic was being kept moving. Another road closure alert was issued for the road from Avari Towers towards Mehran Hotel and Sharea Faisal at 5:10pm. Traffic is being sent via Avari Towers towards Fatima Jinnah Road, police said. Motorists were earlier advised to avoid roads around the KPC and follow the traffic police’s instructions. The public was also urged to cooperate with law enforcement agencies and traffic police. Commuters requiring assistance could contact the Traffic Police Rahnuma helpline at 1915, where representatives would be available round the clock to provide guidance. The latest traffic updates are also available through Karachi Traffic Police’s social media platforms, the statement added.

items.title: Short-term inflation clocks in at 9.49pc driven by wheat flour prices
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Short-term inflation was recorded at 9.49 per cent year-on-year in the week ending on Nov 26, driven largely by wheat flour prices, according to official data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) on Friday. The index comprises 51 items, with prices collected from 50 markets in 17 cities, and is calculated weekly to track changes in the prices of essential commodities and services. The data showed that the prices of 20 commodities increased, while those of nine items declined. Meanwhile, the prices of 22 items remained unchanged from the previous week. Short-term inflation has entered single digits after several weeks owing to a decline in petroleum products prices. It had remained in the double digits for several consecutive weeks, largely due to persistently elevated petrol and diesel prices. During the 25 days leading up to Nov 27, petrol prices fell from Rs396.06 to Rs313 per litre, while diesel prices declined from Rs398.80 to Rs346 per litre. This represented reductions of about Rs83 and Rs52 per litre, respectively. The impact of this decline was visible in the week-on-week review. The Sensitive Price Index (SPI) declined by 0.11pc week-on-week, reflecting declining oil prices. This is the third consecutive week that SPI recorded a marginal decline on a week-on-week basis. However, the provincial governments have yet to take urgent measures to reduce passenger and freight fares in line with the decline in petrol and diesel prices. Due to these high fares, the prices of perishable products are also higher. Meanwhile, the items that recorded the highest price increases over the previous week included wheat flour (5.72pc), electricity for Q1 (5.43pc), eggs (4.36pc), chicken (4.14pc), garlic (1.54pc), rice basmati broken (0.79pc), potatoes (0.78pc), pulse gram (0.57pc), match box (0.47pc), bread plain (0.44pc), firewood (0.24pc) and washing soap (0.19pc). Items that recorded week-on-week price declines included tomatoes (23.92pc), onions (21.27pc), LPG (7.78pc), petrol (2.48pc), diesel (1.99pc), pulse masoor (0.68pc), sugar (0.24pc) and bananas & pulse mash (0.12pc) each. On an annual basis, the items that recorded the highest price increases included LPG (67.49pc), wheat flour (53.53pc), chicken (30.10pc), electricity for Q1 (29.33pc), diesel (22.36pc), petrol (18.34pc), chillies powder (15.55pc), mutton (14.59pc), bread plain (12.85pc), beef (11.09pc), pulse gram (9.62pc) and milk fresh (8.96pc). In contrast, sugar prices fell by 26.56pc, potatoes (23.04pc), tomatoes (15.91pc), eggs (11.78pc), salt powder (8.78pc), pulse moong (7.57pc), pulse masoor (7.29pc) and gur (5.71pc). Last week, short-term inflation was recorded at 10.41pc year-on-year, driven largely by wheat flour prices. Prior to that, short-term inflation rose to 11.21pc year-on-year, driven largely by perishable food products.

items.title: Airline Norse Atlantic's Norwegian operating unit declares bankruptcy
items.description: Airline Norse Atlantic’s Norwegian operating unit has declared bankruptcy, the long-haul budget carrier said on Friday, succumbing to soaring fuel costs wrought by the war on Iran. Norse Atlantic ASA, which is listed on the Oslo Euronext Expand bourse, and other group companies are not part of the filing and are still attempting to stay in business, the company said in a statement. Norse Atlantic, which launched in 2022, on Wednesday warned that its financial situation was “critical” , and the following day said it had suspended all flights and that the board could file for bankruptcy unless it urgently secured funding. Earlier on Friday, Norse said its lessors had terminated their leasing contracts for all 12 aircraft in the carrier’s fleet, demanding that the planes be handed back, a claim contested by the company. “The Board of Norse Atlantic Airways AS has made the difficult decision to file for bankruptcy despite extensive efforts from the company and the group to find a solution,” Norse CEO Eivind Roald said in a statement. “The board, management and advisers of the listed entity Norse Atlantic ASA and the UK subsidiary are working to find a solution for the remaining part of the business to continue operations,” Roald said. The global aviation industry is suffering its worst crisis since the Covid-19 pandemic as the US-Iran conflict, which began at the end of February, disrupts operations, drives up fuel prices, and sends airlines’ costs skyrocketing. Pakistan International Airlines (PIA), a wet-lease partner of the airline, said earlier that it would shift its UK operations to its own Boeing 777 fleet from Nov 26 after Norse Atlantic abruptly suspended operations, forcing the cancellation of two flights from London and Manchester. Norse in 2021 signed long-term leases for nine Boeing 787 Dreamliner aircraft from Ireland-based AerCap Holdings and six Dreamliners from Singapore-based BOC Aviation Ltd. It later returned three of the planes to AerCap. In October, PIA signed an ACMI (aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance) lease agreement with Norse Atlantic Airways to acquire two state-of-the-art Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners, one of which arrived in Islamabad on Nov 1. A PIA spokesperson at the time said the addition of the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner would mark the start of the expansion of the airline’s fleet as it aimed to meet rising demand.
